name: Enhanced physiological tremor (EPT)
formal: Fine, rapid postural tremor of 8 to 12 Hz that is an exaggeration of normal tremor due to anxiety, caffeine, thyrotoxicosis, drugs or fatigue and resolves when the cause is removed.
simple: A fine, fast hand shake that is stronger than usual because of things like caffeine, stress, an overactive thyroid or some medicines.
th: อาการสั่นเร็วละเอียด 8–12 Hz ขณะยกแขน เป็นการขยายของการสั่นปกติจากความวิตกกังวล คาเฟอีน ไทรอยด์เป็นพิษ ยา หรือความเหนื่อยล้า หายเมื่อแก้สาเหตุ
tempoNote: Fluctuates with triggers; resolves when the cause is removed
feat: Fine, fast, symmetric postural tremor of outstretched hands
Worse with anxiety, caffeine, sleep deprivation, fatigue, hypoglycaemia
Causes: thyrotoxicosis, beta-agonists, lithium, valproate, SSRIs, alcohol withdrawal
No other neurological signs
inv: TSH, glucose, calcium
Drug and caffeine review; alcohol history
Accelerometry/EMG if needed (frequency reduces with weight loading)

case.story: Before exams her hands shake when holding a cup; she drinks four coffees a day.
case.exam: Fine symmetric postural tremor of both hands, no other signs; resting pulse 104.
case.tests: TSH suppressed, free T4 high.
case.q: What is the likely cause of her tremor?
case.a: Enhanced physiological tremor from hyperthyroidism, aggravated by caffeine and stress.

read.where: Chapter 9 Movement Disorders — Enhanced Physiological Tremor

det.patho: Everyone has a low-amplitude physiological tremor from mechanical resonance of limbs and reflex loops. Increased beta-adrenergic stimulation of muscle spindles and reflex gain enhances it to a visible level. Mechanical tremor frequency falls with added weight, distinguishing it from central tremors.
det.clinical: Tremor is postural and symmetric, often noticed when holding objects or with fine tasks. It fluctuates with emotional state and stimulants. No other neurological abnormalities are present.
det.diagnosis: Clinical, with a search for triggers: thyroid function, glucose, drug history, caffeine and alcohol. Electrophysiology shows frequency shifting with loading. Persistent tremor without trigger suggests essential tremor.
det.treatment: Remove or treat the cause (e.g. thyroid treatment, reduce caffeine, adjust drugs). Propranolol can be used situationally for performance-related tremor.
det.prognosis: Excellent; resolves with removal of the trigger.
pearls: Check TSH in any new fine tremor.
Frequency drops with weight loading in mechanical tremor.
Performance tremor responds to a single dose of propranolol.
det.thd: Enhanced physiological tremor คือการสั่นละเอียดเร็วทั้งสองมือเวลายกแขน เป็นการสั่นปกติที่ถูกขยายจากความวิตกกังวล คาเฟอีน ไทรอยด์เป็นพิษ ยา หรือการอดนอน ตรวจไทรอยด์ น้ำตาล และทบทวนยา รักษาที่สาเหตุ propranolol ช่วยในสถานการณ์เฉพาะ

ddx.pt: Persistent, progressive, family history, often head and voice involvement
Variable frequency, distractibility and entrainment
Irregular tremor with dystonic posturing and null point

name: Entrapment neuropathies
formal: Focal nerve injuries from compression at anatomical tunnels, such as carpal tunnel, cubital tunnel and fibular head, causing local sensory loss, weakness and slowed conduction across the site.
simple: Nerves pinched at narrow spots in the body, such as the wrist or elbow, causing tingling, numbness or weakness.
th: เส้นประสาทถูกบีบในช่องแคบทางกายวิภาค เช่น carpal tunnel, cubital tunnel, fibular head ทำให้ชา ปวด และอ่อนแรงเฉพาะที่
tempoNote: Gradual onset with intermittent symptoms before constant deficit
feat: Positional or nocturnal paraesthesia in a single nerve distribution
Provocative signs: Tinel, Phalen, elbow flexion test
Later wasting of muscles supplied distal to the site
Risk factors: diabetes, hypothyroidism, pregnancy, repetitive work, obesity, amyloidosis
Bilateral carpal tunnel in older adults can be an early sign of ATTR amyloidosis
inv: Nerve conduction studies localising slowing to the tunnel
High-resolution ultrasound: nerve swelling proximal to the entrapment
Screen for systemic contributors when bilateral or atypical

case.who: 50-year-old female rice farmer from Sakon Nakhon
case.story: Numb thumb, index and middle fingers waking her nightly; she shakes her hand to relieve it.
case.exam: Tinel and Phalen positive at the wrist, mild thenar weakness, sensation over thenar eminence preserved.
case.tests: NCS: prolonged median distal motor and sensory latencies, ulnar normal.
case.q: Why is thenar skin sensation spared?
case.a: The palmar cutaneous branch leaves the median nerve before the carpal tunnel.

read.where: Chapter 16 Diseases of the Peripheral Nerves — Focal and Compressive Neuropathies
3. Common Mononeuropathies of the Lower Extremities
Chapter 18 Thyroid Disease and the Nervous System

det.patho: Chronic compression in a narrow tunnel causes venous congestion, endoneurial oedema and focal demyelination, then axonal loss if prolonged. Tissue swelling (pregnancy, hypothyroidism), deposition (amyloid) or repetitive motion raise tunnel pressure.
det.clinical: Symptoms start intermittently, often at night or with sustained postures, and become constant. Weakness and wasting indicate axon loss and more urgent treatment. Ulnar entrapment at the elbow affects intrinsic hand muscles and the medial hand; fibular entrapment causes foot drop.
det.diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis is confirmed by electrodiagnosis showing focal slowing; ultrasound adds anatomical information. Look for systemic contributors when bilateral or multiple.
det.treatment: Splinting, activity modification and corticosteroid injection help mild to moderate cases. Surgical decompression is offered for persistent symptoms, axon loss or failure of conservative care. Treat underlying diabetes or hypothyroidism.
det.prognosis: Good when treated before significant axonal loss.
pearls: Thenar sensory sparing localises median damage to the wrist.
Bilateral carpal tunnel in older men may herald ATTR amyloidosis.
Wasting signals axonal loss: do not delay surgery.
det.thd: Entrapment neuropathy คือเส้นประสาทถูกบีบในช่องแคบ เช่น carpal tunnel ที่ข้อมือ cubital tunnel ที่ข้อศอก และ fibular head ที่เข่า อาการเริ่มจากชาเป็นพักๆ โดยเฉพาะกลางคืน ต่อมาอ่อนแรงและลีบ ยืนยันด้วย NCS และ ultrasound รักษาด้วยเฝือก ฉีดยา หรือผ่าตัดคลาย และหาโรคร่วม เช่น เบาหวาน ไทรอยด์ amyloid

name: Eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome
formal: Epidemic multisystem illness linked to contaminated L-tryptophan, characterised by severe myalgia, marked eosinophilia, fasciitis, and later sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
simple: A serious illness tied to contaminated tryptophan supplements, causing severe muscle pain and nerve damage.
more: Stop tryptophan; corticosteroids are used. Neuropathy and myalgia may persist for years in many patients.
th: โรคที่เกิดระบาดจากการใช้ L-tryptophan ที่ปนเปื้อน ทำให้ปวดกล้ามเนื้อรุนแรง eosinophil สูง ผิวหนังแข็ง และเส้นประสาทเสื่อม
tempoNote: Acute illness over weeks followed by a chronic phase lasting years
feat: Severe incapacitating myalgia and fatigue
Peripheral eosinophilia above 1000/µL
Skin thickening and fasciitis resembling scleroderma
Later sensorimotor axonal neuropathy, sometimes severe
Historic epidemic in 1989 linked to one manufacturer's L-tryptophan
inv: Full blood count with eosinophil count
Muscle and fascia biopsy: perimysial and fascial inflammation with eosinophils
Nerve conduction: axonal neuropathy

case.who: 44-year-old woman from Bangkok using an imported sleep supplement
case.story: Severe muscle pain, rash and swelling of the forearms over a month; then numb feet.
case.exam: Woody induration of forearm skin, diffuse muscle tenderness, distal sensory loss.
case.tests: Eosinophils 3200/µL; fascia biopsy shows eosinophil-rich fasciitis; supplement contains L-tryptophan.
case.q: What is the first management step?
case.a: Stop the supplement; consider corticosteroids and treat complications.

det.patho: The 1989 epidemic was traced to L-tryptophan from one manufacturer with contaminants formed during production. The illness reflects an immune response with eosinophil activation and tissue infiltration of fascia, muscle, nerve and lung. Sporadic cases still occur occasionally.
det.clinical: The acute phase features myalgia, eosinophilia, rash, oedema, dyspnoea and fever. Chronic phase findings include fasciitis, skin thickening, neuropathy, cognitive complaints and persistent pain. The neuropathy can be severe and occasionally resembles an ascending polyradiculoneuropathy.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis rests on myalgia, eosinophilia and exposure history after excluding infection and neoplasm. Biopsy supports fasciitis and inflammatory myopathy. Electrodiagnosis characterises neuropathy.
det.treatment: Stop the exposure. Corticosteroids may help acute inflammation but have limited effect on chronic features. Symptomatic management of pain and rehabilitation for neuropathy and contractures.
det.prognosis: Many patients had symptoms persisting for years; mortality was low but not negligible.
pearls: Ask about supplements in unexplained eosinophilic myalgia.
Fasciitis with eosinophilia plus neuropathy suggests EMS over Shulman syndrome.
The disease is a toxic-immune model for scleroderma-like illness.
det.thd: EMS เป็นโรคที่ระบาดปี 1989 จากการใช้ L-tryptophan ที่ปนเปื้อน ทำให้ปวดกล้ามเนื้อรุนแรง eosinophil สูง ผิวหนังและ fascia หนาแข็ง และเส้นประสาทเสื่อมตามมา วินิจฉัยจากประวัติการใช้ supplement ร่วมกับผลเลือดและชิ้นเนื้อ รักษาโดยหยุดสาร ใช้ steroid และฟื้นฟู อาการอาจเรื้อรังหลายปี

name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)
formal: ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis in people with asthma and eosinophilia, frequently causing mononeuritis multiplex and occasionally stroke or cranial neuropathy.
simple: An immune disease causing inflamed blood vessels in people with asthma, which can damage nerves and lead to weakness or numbness.
more: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss), an ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis in asthmatic patients causing eosinophilia and mononeuritis multiplex. Blood eosinophilia, p-ANCA in about 40 percent, and nerve or muscle biopsy support it. Treat with corticosteroids with cyclophosphamide, or mepolizumab; relapses are common.
th: vasculitis ชนิด ANCA ในผู้ป่วยหอบหืดที่มี eosinophil สูง มักทำให้เส้นประสาทหลายเส้นเสียแบบ mononeuritis multiplex
tempoNote: Years of asthma and rhinosinusitis, then eosinophilic phase, then vasculitic neuropathy over days to weeks
feat: Adult-onset asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps precede vasculitis
Blood eosinophilia, often over 1500/µL
Mononeuritis multiplex (foot drop, wrist drop) in more than half of patients
Cardiac involvement (myocarditis) is the main cause of death
ANCA (usually MPO) positive in only about 30–40%
inv: FBC with eosinophil count, ANCA, IgE, urinalysis and renal function
NCS/EMG: asymmetric axonal multiple mononeuropathy
Nerve and muscle biopsy: necrotising vasculitis with eosinophils
Cardiac MRI, troponin and echocardiography

case.who: 47-year-old woman from Lampang with asthma for 6 years and nasal polyps
case.story: Two weeks of fever, burning left foot pain, then left foot drop and right hand weakness.
case.exam: Left foot drop, weak right finger abduction, patchy sensory loss in left peroneal and right ulnar territories, scattered purpura.
case.tests: Eosinophils 4,800/µL; MPO-ANCA positive; NCS shows axonal left peroneal and right ulnar neuropathies; sural biopsy shows eosinophil-rich vasculitis.
case.q: What is the diagnosis and the immediate treatment?
case.a: EGPA with vasculitic mononeuritis multiplex; high-dose glucocorticoids plus cyclophosphamide or rituximab for severe disease.

det.patho: EGPA is a small-vessel vasculitis with eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation. Two overlapping mechanisms operate: ANCA-related vasculitis (more renal and neuropathic disease) and eosinophil tissue toxicity (more cardiac and lung disease). IL-5 driven eosinophilia is central, which underlies the use of anti-IL-5 therapy.
det.clinical: The illness evolves through an allergic phase with asthma and sinus disease, an eosinophilic phase with lung infiltrates or gut involvement, and a vasculitic phase with neuropathy, purpura, renal disease and cardiac involvement. Peripheral neuropathy is the commonest neurological feature; CNS involvement such as stroke or cranial neuropathy is uncommon. Leukotriene antagonist use or steroid tapering sometimes unmasks the disease.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis combines asthma, eosinophilia and vasculitic organ involvement, supported by ANCA and biopsy. ACR/EULAR 2022 classification criteria help. Nerve conduction studies document multiple mononeuropathy; taking nerve and muscle together at biopsy raises the diagnostic yield. Exclude parasitic infection (e.g. Strongyloides in Thailand) before high-dose steroids.
det.treatment: Severe disease with neuropathy, cardiac or renal involvement is treated with high-dose glucocorticoids plus cyclophosphamide or rituximab. Mepolizumab or benralizumab (anti-IL-5 pathway) are used for relapsing or refractory non-severe disease and to spare steroids. Neuropathic pain treatment and rehabilitation are needed; nerve recovery is slow.
det.prognosis: Survival is good with treatment, but relapses are common and residual neuropathy is frequent; cardiac disease drives mortality.
pearls: Asthma plus eosinophilia plus foot drop: EGPA until proven otherwise.
ANCA negativity does not exclude EGPA.
Treat empirically for Strongyloides before heavy immunosuppression in endemic areas.
det.thd: EGPA เป็น vasculitis ของหลอดเลือดขนาดเล็กที่มี eosinophil มาก มักเกิดในผู้ที่เป็นหอบหืดและริดสีดวงจมูก อาการทางประสาทที่พบบ่อยคือเส้นประสาทหลายเส้นเสียแบบ mononeuritis multiplex เช่น เท้าตก ANCA บวกเพียงส่วนน้อย วินิจฉัยด้วยระดับ eosinophil, NCS และชิ้นเนื้อ รักษาด้วย steroid ขนาดสูงร่วมกับ cyclophosphamide หรือ rituximab และใช้ mepolizumab ในรายที่กลับเป็นซ้ำ

qx.stem: A 45-year-old woman from Nakhon Pathom with adult-onset asthma and nasal polyps has blood eosinophilia and sudden wrist and foot drop in a mononeuritis multiplex pattern. ANCA is initially reported negative.
qx.q: Which statement is correct?
opts: A negative ANCA does not exclude EGPA, but when neuropathy predominates ANCA is usually positive
ANCA positivity is mandatory for the diagnosis
Eosinophilia is rare and not helpful
CNS vasculitis is the commonest manifestation and nerve involvement is rare
Corticosteroids are contraindicated
qx.why: EGPA combines obstructive airway disease, eosinophilia and necrotising vasculitis with eosinophil-rich granulomas; multiple mononeuropathy is typical. ANCA negativity does not rule it out, and ANCA-negative disease more often involves heart, kidney and gut, whereas ANCA-positive disease more often brings neuropathy. Treatment uses glucocorticoids with rituximab, cyclophosphamide or anti-IL-5 biologics.

formal: Muscle disorders with eosinophilic infiltration, including eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome and focal eosinophilic myositis, causing myalgia, weakness and peripheral eosinophilia.
simple: Muscle conditions in which a type of white blood cell builds up in the muscles, causing pain and weakness.

det.patho: Eosinophils release cytotoxic granule proteins that damage muscle fibres, fascia and vessels. Triggers include helminth infection, drugs and toxins, clonal or idiopathic hypereosinophilia and systemic vasculitis. In some genetic dystrophies eosinophils appear secondarily during early necrosis.
det.clinical: This heading groups conditions rather than one disease. Focal eosinophilic myositis gives a painful swollen calf; diffuse eosinophilic polymyositis gives proximal weakness with systemic features; perimyositis causes myalgia and fascial swelling. Trichinosis in Thailand typically follows eating raw or undercooked pork or wild boar and causes fever, periorbital oedema and myalgia. Cardiac involvement is the main danger.
det.diagnosis: Blood eosinophilia plus myositis prompts a search for parasites, drugs and haematological or vasculitic disease. MRI shows oedema in muscle and fascia. Biopsy demonstrates eosinophilic infiltrates and sometimes larvae. Echocardiography and troponin screen for myocarditis.
det.treatment: Treat the cause: anthelmintics for parasites, drug withdrawal, management of hypereosinophilic syndrome or EGPA. Corticosteroids are used for idiopathic or severe inflammatory forms. If a dystrophy such as calpainopathy is found, immunotherapy is not helpful.
det.prognosis: Generally favourable when the cause is treated; cardiac involvement worsens outlook.
pearls: Raw pork, fever, periorbital oedema and myalgia: think trichinosis.
Eosinophilic myositis in a teenager can be the first sign of calpainopathy.
Always check the heart when eosinophils are high.
det.thd: Eosinophilic myopathy เป็นกลุ่มโรคที่มี eosinophil แทรกในกล้ามเนื้อหรือเยื่อหุ้มกล้ามเนื้อ ทำให้ปวด บวม และอ่อนแรง สาเหตุสำคัญในไทยคือพยาธิ เช่น trichinosis จากการกินหมูดิบ นอกจากนี้มียา hypereosinophilic syndrome และ EGPA วินิจฉัยด้วยผลเลือด eosinophil CK MRI และชิ้นเนื้อ รักษาตามสาเหตุ และใช้ steroid ในรายที่รุนแรง

det.patho: Eosinophils infiltrate muscle and release toxic granule proteins, causing necrosis and inflammation. The trigger may be parasitic larvae, systemic hypereosinophilia, vasculitis or drugs. Some genetic dystrophies (calpain-3) show eosinophilic infiltrates early.
det.clinical: Presentation ranges from focal myositis to diffuse painful weakness. Systemic features (fever, rash, oedema, cardiac involvement) depend on the cause. Parasitic disease follows ingestion of undercooked meat.
det.diagnosis: Combine eosinophil count, CK, parasite tests, ANCA and muscle biopsy. MRI shows oedema. Look for cardiac involvement. Genetic testing if biopsy suggests dystrophy.
det.treatment: Treat the cause: antiparasitic therapy, withdraw culprit drugs, immunosuppression for HES or EGPA. Corticosteroids are commonly used to reduce inflammation.
det.prognosis: Generally good when the cause is treated; cardiac involvement worsens prognosis.
pearls: Ask about raw pork or wild boar in Thai patients with myalgia and eosinophilia.

Eosinophils on biopsy in a young patient may signal calpain-3 dystrophy.

name: Ependymomas
formal: Glial tumours arising from ependymal cells lining the ventricles or central canal, typically in the posterior fossa in children or the spinal cord in adults, causing hydrocephalus or myelopathy.
simple: Brain or spinal cord tumours growing from cells lining the fluid spaces, which can block fluid flow or press on the spinal cord.
th: เนื้องอกจากเซลล์เยื่อบุโพรงสมอง พบบ่อยในเด็กที่ช่องสมองที่ 4 ทำให้น้ำคั่งสมอง ปวดศีรษะ อาเจียน ส่วนในผู้ใหญ่พบในไขสันหลัง การผ่าตัดเอาออกให้หมดคือปัจจัยพยากรณ์ที่สำคัญที่สุด ตามด้วยฉายรังสีเฉพาะที่
tempoNote: Weeks to months of headache, vomiting and ataxia in the posterior fossa form; spinal tumours may take years; a longer symptomatic interval has been linked with better outcome
feat: Posterior fossa tumours of children: hydrocephalus with headache, projectile vomiting (sometimes mistaken for gastrointestinal disease), papilloedema, truncal ataxia, diplopia and head tilt or neck stiffness from tonsillar descent
Growth out of the lateral foramen (Luschka) into the CP angle causes lower cranial nerve palsies; extension through Magendie gives neck pain
Supratentorial tumours are large, intraventricular or parenchymal, with seizures, focal signs and raised pressure; adults more often have spinal ependymomas (cervical or lumbar myxopapillary)
WHO CNS5 groups by site and molecule: supratentorial ZFTA- or YAP1-fusion, posterior fossa group A and B, spinal (MYCN-amplified subtype), with myxopapillary grade 2 and subependymoma grade 1
CSF seeding at diagnosis is uncommon (about 10%), more likely with infratentorial, high-grade, young-age or subtotally resected tumours
inv: MRI of brain and whole spine (before surgery or 2 weeks after to avoid blood artefact): heterogeneous enhancing mass in the fourth ventricle extruding through foramina, calcification and cysts, cleavage plane from brainstem
CT: calcification in up to half; hyperdense compared with cerebellar cortex
Histology: perivascular pseudorosettes, true ependymal rosettes, GFAP and EMA dot-like staining; molecular classification (ZFTA/RELA fusion, H3 K27me3 loss for PFA, DNA methylation)
CSF cytology 2 weeks after surgery; lumbar puncture only when herniation risk is excluded

case.story: Eight weeks of vomiting each morning, treated as gastroenteritis, with recent head tilt to the left and clumsy walking.
case.exam: Papilloedema, head tilt, truncal ataxia, left lower motor neuron facial palsy.
case.tests: MRI shows a heterogeneous mass filling the fourth ventricle, that protrudes via the left lateral foramen (Luschka) into the CP angle, with hydrocephalus; spine MRI clear. Gross total resection: ependymoma, posterior fossa group A, H3 K27me3 lost, CNS WHO grade 3.
case.q: What treatment follows complete resection, and why is radiotherapy timing a concern at this age?
case.a: Focal radiotherapy (about 54-59.4 Gy) to the tumour bed, ideally after age 12-18 months; whole-neuraxis radiation is used only when disseminated. Younger children risk growth, endocrine and cognitive effects, so chemotherapy may bridge the interval.

det.patho: Ependymomas arise from ependymal cells or radial glia lining the ventricles and central canal. In children, posterior fossa tumours form two groups: group A (PFA, hypermethylated, loss of H3 K27me3, young age, poor prognosis) and group B (PFB, older patients, good prognosis). Supratentorial tumours often contain ZFTA (C11orf95)-RELA fusions or YAP1 fusions. Spinal ependymomas show NF2 alteration and, rarely, MYCN amplification. The old WHO grade II/III histologic separation correlates poorly with outcome; molecular groups and extent of resection predict it better.
det.clinical: Children present with raised pressure, ataxia and cranial nerve signs; infants may show only rapid head enlargement. Vomiting may dominate and prompt gastrointestinal work-up first. Adults with intracranial ependymoma have headache, diplopia, hemiparesis and seizures; lateral ventricle tumours can cause cognitive decline. Rare patients bleed into the tumour. Seeding of the neuraxis is largely a feature of recurrence.
det.diagnosis: MRI with contrast defines the tumour, usually a soft heterogeneous mass in the fourth ventricle extending through the foramina; the whole spine is imaged before surgery or after two weeks. Histology (pseudorosettes, ependymal canals) and molecular profiling classify the tumour. CSF cytology is taken after surgery. The differential diagnosis includes medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, choroid plexus tumour and AT/RT in infants.
det.treatment: Complete resection is the strongest prognostic factor: five-year survival with gross total resection was reported at about 88 percent versus 53 percent with subtotal in the book's series. Second-look surgery is justified if residual tumour can be removed safely. Post-operative focal radiotherapy is standard for children over 12-18 months and for incompletely resected or anaplastic tumours; craniospinal radiotherapy is reserved for disseminated disease. Chemotherapy has a limited effect (response about 20 percent) but may delay radiotherapy in infants. Hydrocephalus is treated by removing the tumour, with ventriculoperitoneal shunt needed in 30-50 percent. Targeted agents for ZFTA-RELA fusion and PFA ependymoma remain in trials.
det.prognosis: Five-year survival is about 70-85 percent after complete resection and radiotherapy; PFA, young age, incomplete resection and 1q gain are poor features.
pearls: Persistent early-morning vomiting with ataxia in a young child should prompt neuroimaging before a long GI work-up.
Head tilt and neck stiffness with a fourth-ventricle tumour suggest tonsillar descent; avoid lumbar puncture.
Extent of resection outweighs histologic grade as a prognostic factor.
det.thd: Ependymoma เป็นเนื้องอกจากเซลล์เยื่อบุโพรงสมอง พบในเด็กที่ posterior fossa ทำให้ปวดศีรษะ อาเจียนช่วงเช้า เดินเซ และคอเอียง MRI พบก้อนในช่องสมองที่ 4 ที่ยื่นออกทางรูต่าง ๆ ผ่าตัดเอาออกให้หมดคือสิ่งสำคัญที่สุด ตามด้วยฉายรังสีเฉพาะที่ ส่วนเด็กเล็กมากอาจใช้เคมีบำบัดเพื่อเลื่อนการฉายรังสี ปัจจุบันจำแนก PFA/PFB และ ZFTA fusion ตาม WHO 2021 เพื่อประเมินพยากรณ์โรค

det.patho: EPC arises from a small, persistently hyperexcitable area of sensorimotor cortex. The focus may be too small or deep to show on scalp EEG. Causes vary by age: Rasmussen encephalitis and mitochondrial disease in children; stroke, tumours, metabolic derangement and autoimmune encephalitis in adults.
det.clinical: Jerks are usually distal and may be rhythmic or irregular, increased by action or sensory stimulation. Patients remain aware. Untreated, EPC can last for long periods and may cause progressive weakness, especially in Rasmussen encephalitis. Acute onset in an elderly diabetic suggests hyperglycaemia.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis is clinical, supported by EEG, which may show focal discharges or nothing. Jerk-locked back-averaging and EMG help confirm cortical origin. MRI identifies structural lesions. Blood glucose, sodium and osmolality should be checked immediately. In younger patients consider POLG testing, autoimmune antibodies and serial MRI for Rasmussen-type atrophy.
det.treatment: Treat the cause first: correct hyperglycaemia, remove or treat lesions, immunotherapy for autoimmune causes. Antiseizure medicines such as levetiracetam, lacosamide or perampanel can reduce jerks but complete control is often not achieved; aggressive anaesthetic treatment is usually not justified for isolated EPC. Hemispherotomy is considered in Rasmussen encephalitis. Avoid valproate in suspected POLG.
det.prognosis: Depends on cause: metabolic EPC resolves with correction, whereas structural and Rasmussen-related EPC can persist for years.
pearls: Check glucose immediately in any elderly patient with continuous focal jerking.
A normal scalp EEG does not exclude EPC.
Do not escalate to coma induction for EPC alone without strong reason.

name: Epilepsy
formal: Chronic brain disorder with a predisposition to unprovoked recurrent seizures from abnormal synchronised neuronal discharge, with structural, genetic, infectious, metabolic, immune or unknown causes.
simple: A condition in which the brain repeatedly sends abnormal electrical signals, causing seizures that happen without an obvious trigger.
th: โรคสมองที่มีแนวโน้มชักซ้ำโดยไม่มีปัจจัยกระตุ้น จากการปล่อยกระแสไฟฟ้าผิดปกติของเซลล์ประสาท

case.story: Second generalised convulsion in 6 months, both after all-night study; also has morning jerks that make her drop her phone.
case.exam: Normal; tongue bite on the side.
case.tests: EEG shows generalised 4–6 Hz polyspike-wave with photosensitivity; MRI normal.
case.q: What epilepsy type is this, and which medicine choice needs care in women of child-bearing potential?
case.a: Generalised epilepsy (juvenile myoclonic epilepsy); valproate is effective but teratogenic, so levetiracetam or lamotrigine are usually preferred.

det.patho: Seizures arise from excessive, synchronised neuronal firing caused by an imbalance of excitation and inhibition in cortical networks. Lesions such as hippocampal sclerosis, scars, tumours and malformations create focal epileptogenic zones, while genetic variants in ion channels and synaptic proteins underlie many generalised epilepsies. Infection, including neurocysticercosis, is an important cause in Southeast Asia.
det.clinical: Presentation depends on seizure type and syndrome. Focal seizures reflect the region involved and may spread to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures. Generalised epilepsies typically start in childhood or adolescence. Status epilepticus, injuries, psychiatric comorbidity, stigma and driving and employment issues are major concerns.
det.diagnosis: Epilepsy is a clinical diagnosis based on history from the patient and witness; EEG and MRI support classification and cause but a normal EEG does not exclude it. Exclude provoked seizures (hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, alcohol withdrawal) and mimics such as syncope, functional seizures, migraine and sleep disorders. Classify by seizure type, epilepsy type, syndrome and cause.
det.treatment: Start antiseizure medication after a second unprovoked seizure or after a first seizure with high recurrence risk. Choose by seizure type and patient factors: levetiracetam, lamotrigine or valproate for generalised epilepsy (avoid valproate in women of child-bearing potential where possible); lamotrigine, levetiracetam, carbamazepine or lacosamide for focal epilepsy. About a third become drug-resistant after two appropriate drugs; refer for presurgical evaluation, neuromodulation or diet therapy. Counsel on safety, driving, contraception and SUDEP.
det.prognosis: About two-thirds become seizure-free on medication; many children with self-limited syndromes outgrow their epilepsy.
pearls: Always get an ECG after a first convulsion to exclude cardiac syncope.
Two appropriate drug failures = drug-resistant epilepsy: refer for surgical evaluation.
Carbamazepine and phenytoin can worsen absence and myoclonic seizures; HLA-B*15:02 testing before carbamazepine in Thai patients.

qx.stem: A 58-year-old accountant fainted while standing in a long queue at a temple fair, with a few brief jerks and rapid recovery. Neurological examination is normal. A routine EEG reports arciform 7–10 Hz trains with sharply contoured negative peaks over the left then right mid-temporal region during drowsiness, without any following slow wave or background disturbance; the trains are not seen in full wakefulness.
qx.q: What is the best interpretation?
opts: Left temporal lobe epilepsy; start levetiracetam
Wicket rhythm, a benign variant; manage the episode as probable reflex syncope
Periodic lateralised discharges requiring urgent MRI and admission
Small sharp spikes indicating generalized epilepsy
Breach rhythm from an unrecognised skull defect
qx.why: Wicket rhythm consists of arch-shaped mid-temporal waves in adults, alternating sides, in drowsiness, lacking an aftergoing slow wave or background disruption; it is a benign variant frequently over-read as epileptiform. The history fits reflex syncope with convulsive jerks. Treating the EEG rather than the patient leads to epilepsy misdiagnosis and unnecessary drugs.

qx.stem: A 33-year-old motorcycle taxi driver in Khon Kaen has his first ever bilateral tonic-clonic seizure while asleep. He took no drugs or alcohol, electrolytes and glucose are normal, and the neurological examination is normal. A 3 T MRI is unremarkable, but a sleep-deprived EEG shows repeated left anterior temporal sharp waves.
qx.q: Which statement best guides the discussion with him today?
opts: With a single seizure he cannot have epilepsy, so treatment should wait for a second event
His recurrence risk is below 20%, so a repeat EEG in a year is all that is needed
The EEG finding raises his recurrence risk enough to meet the practical definition of epilepsy, and starting an antiseizure medication is reasonable after shared decision-making
Immediate treatment will improve his chance of long-term remission compared with deferred treatment
He should start two antiseizure medications because the discharges are focal
qx.why: Under the 2014 ILAE practical definition, one unprovoked seizure plus a recurrence risk of about 60% (here driven by epileptiform discharges) counts as epilepsy. Early treatment roughly halves the near-term recurrence risk but trials such as FIRST and MESS showed no gain in long-term remission, so the decision is shared and weighs things like his occupation and driving. Two drugs from the start are never indicated.

qx.stem: A 32-year-old man with multifocal drug-resistant focal epilepsy is not a candidate for resection. He has a past episode of major depression, now in remission on sertraline. The team is weighing a vagal nerve stimulator against anterior thalamic (ANT) deep brain stimulation.
qx.q: Which statement is most accurate for counseling him?
opts: Anterior thalamic DBS has been linked to self-reported depression and memory complaints, so mood should be monitored closely
VNS usually works fully within the first week, and benefit then fades
Hoarseness and cough during stimulation are typical of anterior thalamic DBS
Neither device ever allows MRI afterwards
DBS needs no surgical implantation
qx.why: In the SANTE trial of anterior thalamic DBS, seizures fell progressively over years, but depression and subjective memory problems were reported more often, which matters given his history. Voice change, cough and throat discomfort during on-cycles are typical of VNS, whose benefit also grows over 1–2 years rather than fading. Both devices allow MRI under specific manufacturer conditions.

det.patho: Epileptic myoclonus results from hyperexcitable sensorimotor cortex producing a brief synchronous discharge that travels down corticospinal pathways. In generalised epilepsies it reflects thalamocortical network hyperexcitability; in progressive myoclonic epilepsies it reflects neuronal loss of inhibition from storage or degenerative disease. Cortical reflex myoclonus, triggered by touch or movement, shows enlarged sensory evoked responses.
det.clinical: Jerks are brief, often bilateral and may cause dropping objects or falls. They occur without obvious loss of consciousness, so patients may not report them unless asked directly. Progressive forms add ataxia, cognitive decline and drug-resistant seizures.
det.diagnosis: Clinical recognition plus EEG showing spikes or polyspikes temporally linked to jerks. Neurophysiology can distinguish cortical from subcortical or functional myoclonus. A progressive course needs evaluation for Unverricht–Lundborg disease, Lafora disease, neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses, MERRF and sialidosis.
det.treatment: Valproate, levetiracetam, clonazepam, perampanel and piracetam reduce epileptic myoclonus; brivaracetam and zonisamide are alternatives. Avoid carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, gabapentin and pregabalin, which may aggravate it. Lifestyle measures — regular sleep and limited alcohol — are important.
det.prognosis: In JME myoclonus is usually well controlled but treatment is often lifelong; progressive myoclonic epilepsies carry a poor prognosis.
pearls: Ask specifically about morning jerks in any young person with a first convulsion.
Sodium-channel blockers can worsen myoclonus.
Myoclonus plus progressive ataxia or dementia: think progressive myoclonic epilepsy.
det.thd: Epileptic myoclonus คือการกระตุกสั้น ๆ เหมือนไฟช็อตที่เกิดจาก cortex ไวเกินในโรคลมชัก พบบ่อยใน JME ซึ่งกระตุกมากตอนเช้าหรือเมื่ออดนอน EEG พบ spike หรือ polyspike ตรงกับการกระตุก รักษาด้วย valproate, levetiracetam หรือ clonazepam และควรหลีกเลี่ยง carbamazepine หรือ phenytoin ที่อาจทำให้แย่ลง ถ้ามีเดินเซหรือสมองเสื่อมร่วมด้วยให้นึกถึง progressive myoclonic epilepsy

det.patho: Syndromes reflect the interaction of age-dependent brain maturation, genetic susceptibility and acquired lesions. Many generalised syndromes have polygenic inheritance, while early-onset encephalopathies often have single-gene causes. The 2022 ILAE framework classifies syndromes by age at onset and as self-limited, generalised, focal, or with developmental/epileptic encephalopathy.
det.clinical: Identifying a syndrome answers practical questions: likely response to particular drugs, chance of remission, need for imaging or genetic tests and associated learning or behavioural problems. Many patients do not fit a named syndrome and are classified by seizure and epilepsy type instead.
det.diagnosis: Requires integrating history, video of events, EEG and imaging; mandatory and exclusionary criteria for each syndrome are published by ILAE. Reassess when the course does not follow the expected pattern, such as an absence epilepsy that fails to remit or regresses.
det.treatment: Treatment is tailored: ethosuximide for childhood absence, levetiracetam, lamotrigine or valproate for JME, steroids or vigabatrin for infantile spasms, and observation without drugs may be reasonable in SeLECTS with rare seizures. Avoid drugs known to worsen a syndrome (e.g. sodium-channel blockers in Dravet or absence epilepsy). Refractory syndromes may need diet, surgery or neuromodulation.
det.prognosis: Varies widely: self-limited syndromes usually remit by adolescence, whereas DEEs have lifelong seizures and disability.
pearls: Name the syndrome when possible — it guides drug choice and prognosis.
Hyperventilation in clinic can reproduce absence seizures.
Typical rolandic epilepsy often needs no medicine.
det.thd: Epileptic syndromes คือกลุ่มลมชักที่จำแนกตามอายุที่เริ่ม ชนิดการชัก EEG และสาเหตุ เช่น childhood absence epilepsy, SeLECTS, West, Lennox–Gastaut และ JME การระบุกลุ่มอาการช่วยเลือกยาที่เหมาะสมและหลีกเลี่ยงยาที่ทำให้แย่ลง รวมถึงคาดการณ์ว่าโรคจะหายเองหรือเป็นตลอดชีวิต ใช้ประวัติ วิดีโอ EEG และภาพถ่ายสมองร่วมกันในการวินิจฉัย

det.patho: EA1 results from variants in KCNA1, encoding the Kv1.1 potassium channel, causing hyperexcitability in cerebellar basket cells and peripheral nerves (myokymia). EA2 results mainly from loss-of-function CACNA1A variants of the Cav2.1 (P/Q) channel in Purkinje cells, leading to irregular Purkinje firing. Other EA types involve CACNB4, SLC1A3, UBR4 and others.
det.clinical: EA1 begins in childhood with very brief attacks of ataxia provoked by sudden movement, startle or emotion, with continuous myokymia around the eyes or hands between attacks. EA2 attacks are longer and often accompanied by vertigo, nausea, diplopia and headache; many patients develop interictal nystagmus and slowly progressive ataxia. Some families also have epilepsy or hemiplegic migraine.
det.diagnosis: Attack duration and triggers suggest the type. Interictal examination for myokymia (EA1) or nystagmus (EA2) is useful. Genetic testing confirms the diagnosis. Alternative causes of paroxysmal ataxia, such as MS paroxysms, posterior circulation TIA, metabolic defects and drug toxicity, should be considered when features are atypical.
det.treatment: Acetazolamide reduces attack frequency in many with EA2 and some with EA1. 4-aminopyridine (fampridine) is effective in EA2 and is an alternative. Carbamazepine or other sodium-channel blockers can help EA1. Trigger avoidance is advised.
det.prognosis: Normal life expectancy; EA2 may lead to persistent mild ataxia.
pearls: Seconds with myokymia = EA1; hours with nystagmus = EA2.
CACNA1A links EA2, familial hemiplegic migraine type 1 and SCA6.
Acetazolamide and 4-aminopyridine are the main drugs for EA2.
det.thd: Episodic ataxia เป็นโรคช่องไอออนถ่ายทอดแบบยีนเด่น ทำให้เดินเซเป็นพัก ๆ EA1 จากยีน KCNA1 เป็นสั้นไม่กี่วินาทีถึงนาทีและมี myokymia ส่วน EA2 จากยีน CACNA1A เป็นนานหลายชั่วโมงร่วมกับเวียนหัวอาเจียน และมี nystagmus ระหว่างพัก รักษาด้วย acetazolamide หรือ 4-aminopyridine และหลีกเลี่ยงสิ่งกระตุ้น

det.patho: KCNA1 codes for Kv1.1, a voltage-dependent K+ channel expressed in cerebellar basket cells and in peripheral nerve terminals. Reduced potassium current makes neurons hyperexcitable, producing transient cerebellar dysfunction and continuous motor unit activity in nerves. Inheritance is autosomal dominant.
det.clinical: Attacks begin in childhood, usually lasting seconds to a few minutes, and may occur many times daily. Triggers are abrupt movement, startle, exertion or emotional stress. Between attacks, patients have myokymia, and some have muscle stiffness or epilepsy. Attacks may lessen in adulthood.
det.diagnosis: The diagnosis is clinical, supported by EMG demonstration of myokymia and confirmed by KCNA1 testing. Brain MRI is normal. Exclude epilepsy, paroxysmal dyskinesias and other episodic ataxias.
det.treatment: Avoiding triggers helps. Carbamazepine, acetazolamide or other anticonvulsants reduce attack frequency in some. Treatment response is variable, and evidence is from small series.
det.prognosis: Not usually progressive; attacks often diminish with age.
pearls: Seconds-long ataxic attacks plus myokymia point to EA1.
EMG between attacks is the most useful test.
EA2 is the commoner episodic ataxia and has interictal nystagmus.
det.thd: Episodic ataxia type 1 เป็นโรคพันธุกรรมแบบเด่นจากยีน KCNA1 ช่องโพแทสเซียม ทำให้เดินเซและพูดไม่ชัดเป็นช่วงสั้น ๆ เพียงวินาทีถึงนาที กระตุ้นด้วยการเคลื่อนไหวทันทีหรือการตกใจ ระหว่างช่วงไม่มีอาการพบกล้ามเนื้อกระตุกระริก (myokymia) วินิจฉัยด้วย EMG และตรวจยีน รักษาด้วยการเลี่ยงสิ่งกระตุ้นและยาอย่าง carbamazepine

det.patho: Loss-of-function variants in CACNA1A reduce P/Q-type calcium current in cerebellar Purkinje cells, leading to irregular pacemaking and unstable cerebellar output. Gain-of-function variants in the same gene cause familial hemiplegic migraine, and small CAG expansions cause SCA6. Many variants are truncating or missense; de novo cases occur.
det.clinical: Attacks are stereotyped, lasting hours and occasionally days, with vertigo, nausea and gross ataxia. Between attacks patients may be normal or show nystagmus and mild ataxia. Comorbid migraine, absence epilepsy, dystonia and cognitive problems are reported, especially in children. Slow progression of ataxia over decades is common.
det.diagnosis: Genetic testing confirms the diagnosis, which is suspected from the clinical picture and the family history. EA2 is the most common episodic ataxia. Exclude multiple sclerosis, vestibular migraine and metabolic episodic ataxias in sporadic cases.
det.treatment: Acetazolamide (typically 250–500 mg twice daily in adults) reduces attacks in many; side effects include paraesthesia and kidney stones. 4-aminopyridine is effective in a randomised trial. Avoid triggers and treat comorbid migraine.
det.prognosis: Normal lifespan; some develop slowly progressive permanent ataxia.
pearls: Hours-long attacks plus interictal downbeat nystagmus — think EA2.
CACNA1A links EA2, FHM1 and SCA6.
Acetazolamide response supports the diagnosis.
det.thd: Episodic ataxia type 2 เป็นโรคพันธุกรรมยีนเด่นจากยีน CACNA1A ที่ทำให้ calcium channel ใน Purkinje cell ทำงานลดลง ผู้ป่วยมีอาการเดินเซ พูดไม่ชัด เวียนหัว อาเจียนเป็นพักนานหลายชั่วโมง ระหว่างช่วงปกติพบ downbeat nystagmus เกี่ยวข้องกับ FHM1 และ SCA6 วินิจฉัยด้วยตรวจยีน รักษาด้วย acetazolamide หรือ 4-aminopyridine

name: Episodic vertigo
formal: Recurrent spells of vertigo from vestibular migraine, Meniere disease, BPPV, vertebrobasilar ischaemia or episodic ataxia, distinguished by duration, triggers and associated auditory or neurological features.
simple: Repeated attacks of a spinning sensation that come and go, with causes ranging from inner ear problems to migraine.
th: อาการบ้านหมุนเป็นพักๆ ซ้ำๆ จากหลายสาเหตุ เช่น BPPV, vestibular migraine, Ménière disease, TIA ของระบบ vertebrobasilar
tempoNote: Attack duration is the key discriminator: seconds (BPPV), minutes (TIA), minutes-hours (migraine), hours (Ménière)
feat: A symptom category rather than a single disease
Seconds, triggered by head position: BPPV
Minutes, with other brainstem symptoms or vascular risk: vertebrobasilar TIA
Minutes to hours with headache, photophobia or migraine history: vestibular migraine
Hours, with ear fullness, ringing and fluctuating hearing: Ménière disease
inv: Dix-Hallpike and supine roll tests
Audiometry for low-frequency sensorineural loss
MRI/MRA brain if TIA-like features or vascular risk
Video head impulse and caloric testing in selected patients

case.who: 39-year-old office worker from Bangkok with migraine since her teens
case.story: For a year she has had spells of spinning lasting 20 minutes to 2 hours, sometimes with headache and light sensitivity; no hearing change.
case.exam: Normal between attacks, including Dix-Hallpike and head impulse tests.
case.tests: Audiometry normal; MRI brain normal.
case.q: Which cause of episodic vertigo fits best?
case.a: Vestibular migraine.

20 Migraine and other episodic vestibular disorders

det.patho: Recurrent vertigo results from transient asymmetry in vestibular input. Mechanisms include otoconia displaced into a semicircular canal (BPPV), endolymphatic hydrops (Ménière), migraine-related dysfunction of central and peripheral vestibular pathways, transient ischaemia of brainstem or labyrinth, and channelopathies (episodic ataxia).
det.clinical: Taking a careful history of trigger, duration and associated symptoms is the most useful step. BPPV attacks last under a minute and are positional. Vestibular migraine lasts minutes to days with migraine features in at least half of episodes. Ménière attacks last 20 minutes to 12 hours with ear symptoms. Vertebrobasilar TIA may present with isolated vertigo in a minority, more often with diplopia, dysarthria or ataxia. Panic and orthostatic dizziness are other episodic causes.
det.diagnosis: Bárány Society criteria guide diagnosis of BPPV, vestibular migraine and Ménière disease. Bedside positional testing is essential. Audiometry supports Ménière. Vascular imaging is warranted when TIA is suspected, especially in older patients with risk factors. Inter-attack examination is often normal.
det.treatment: Treatment is cause-specific: repositioning manoeuvres for BPPV, migraine lifestyle measures and preventives for vestibular migraine, salt restriction and betahistine or intratympanic therapy for Ménière, and secondary stroke prevention for TIA. Vestibular suppressants are for short-term use only. Vestibular rehabilitation helps residual imbalance.
det.prognosis: Generally favourable except when episodes are vascular warnings, which carry stroke risk.
pearls: Ask timing, triggers and accompanying symptoms rather than the exact quality of dizziness.
Recurrent brief vertigo plus vascular risk factors in the elderly: consider posterior circulation TIA.
Vestibular migraine is the commonest cause of spontaneous episodic vertigo in younger adults.
det.thd: Episodic vertigo คืออาการบ้านหมุนเป็นพักๆ ซ้ำๆ ซึ่งเป็นกลุ่มอาการ ไม่ใช่โรคเดียว ระยะเวลาที่เป็นช่วยแยกสาเหตุ เช่น ไม่กี่วินาทีตามท่าศีรษะคือ BPPV หลายนาทีอาจเป็น TIA หลายนาทีถึงชั่วโมงร่วมกับปวดศีรษะคือ vestibular migraine และหลายชั่วโมงร่วมกับหูอื้อเสียงในหูคือ Ménière disease การรักษาขึ้นกับสาเหตุ

name: Erdheim–Chester disease (ECD)
formal: Non-Langerhans histiocytosis, often BRAF V600E-mutated, with bone sclerosis, retroperitoneal fibrosis and CNS involvement causing cerebellar ataxia, diabetes insipidus, orbital masses and pyramidal signs.
simple: A rare disease where abnormal immune cells build up in bones and other organs, sometimes the brain, causing unsteadiness and other problems.
more: Rare non-Langerhans histiocytosis with xanthomatous infiltration of bones, retroperitoneum and CNS; causes ataxia, diabetes insipidus and exophthalmos; BRAF V600E may be present. Erdheim-Chester disease: non-Langerhans histiocytosis with bone sclerosis, diabetes insipidus, retroperitoneal fibrosis and CNS lesions, with BRAF V600E mutation in many.
th: histiocytosis ชนิดไม่ใช่ Langerhans ซึ่งเป็นเนื้องอกเม็ดเลือดชนิดหนึ่ง มักมี BRAF V600E แทรกซึมกระดูก รอบไต และสมอง ทำให้เดินเซ เบาจืด และตาโปน
tempoNote: Insidious over months to years; most diagnosed in the 40s–60s
feat: Progressive cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria from dentate and brainstem infiltration
Central diabetes insipidus, often years before diagnosis
Bilateral exophthalmos from retro-orbital masses
Symmetric sclerosis of long-bone metaphyses with bone pain
Hairy kidney appearance (perirenal infiltration), coated aorta, pericardial disease
inv: MRI brain: dentate, pontine, pituitary stalk or dural lesions; orbital masses
Bone scan or PET-CT showing symmetric long-bone uptake; CT chest-abdomen for perirenal and aortic involvement
Biopsy: CD68+, CD1a-negative foamy histiocytes; BRAF V600E and MAPK pathway testing

case.story: Thirsty and passing large urine volumes for five years; over the last year his walking has become unsteady and his eyes bulge.
case.exam: Bilateral proptosis, scanning speech, limb and gait ataxia.
case.tests: MRI shows symmetric dentate nucleus lesions; CT shows rind of soft tissue around both kidneys; bone scan with symmetric knee uptake.
case.q: What unifying diagnosis and targeted treatment should be considered?
case.a: Erdheim–Chester disease; biopsy for BRAF V600E and treat with a BRAF inhibitor such as vemurafenib (or a MEK inhibitor if BRAF-wildtype).

det.patho: ECD is a clonal myeloid neoplasm of histiocytes driven by MAPK pathway mutations, most often BRAF V600E (about half), with others in MAP2K1, KRAS or NRAS. Lipid-laden histiocytes infiltrate tissues with fibrosis and chronic inflammation. Overlap with Langerhans cell histiocytosis occurs in a minority.
det.clinical: Almost every organ can be involved. Neurological disease affects up to half and is a major cause of disability: cerebellar and pyramidal syndromes, diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism, orbital disease, dural masses resembling meningioma and, rarely, spinal involvement. Cardiovascular infiltration (right atrial pseudotumour, periaortic sheathing) and retroperitoneal fibrosis cause serious morbidity.
det.diagnosis: Combine typical imaging (bilateral metaphyseal sclerosis, perirenal infiltration) with biopsy showing CD68+/CD163+, CD1a-negative histiocytes, and test for BRAF V600E and other MAPK mutations. Baseline brain and orbital MRI, cardiac MRI, PET-CT and endocrine testing are recommended. Clinical suspicion is often delayed for years.
det.treatment: BRAF inhibitors (vemurafenib, dabrafenib) for BRAF V600E disease and MEK inhibitors (cobimetinib, trametinib) for other MAPK mutations give high response rates, including in the CNS. Interferon-alpha was the previous standard. Desmopressin treats diabetes insipidus. Treatment is usually long-term because disease relapses after stopping.
det.prognosis: Targeted therapy has markedly improved survival; CNS and cardiac involvement remain adverse factors.
pearls: Diabetes insipidus plus ataxia plus bone pain: think ECD.
Symmetric dentate nucleus lesions on MRI are a classic CNS pattern.
Always test biopsy tissue for BRAF V600E — it directs therapy.
det.thd: Erdheim–Chester disease เป็นเนื้องอกของ histiocyte ชนิดไม่ใช่ Langerhans มักพบการกลายพันธุ์ BRAF V600E เซลล์ไปแทรกในกระดูกยาว รอบไต หัวใจ และสมอง ทำให้เดินเซ เบาจืด ตาโปน วินิจฉัยด้วยภาพกระดูกและชิ้นเนื้อร่วมตรวจยีน รักษาด้วยยามุ่งเป้า BRAF หรือ MEK inhibitor ซึ่งได้ผลดีแม้ในสมอง

qx.stem: A 55-year-old man has diabetes insipidus, bone pain in both legs and a cerebellar syndrome. MRI shows symmetric brainstem and dentate nucleus T2 hyperintensity. Imaging shows 'hairy kidney' perinephric infiltration, and bone scintigraphy shows symmetric long-bone uptake. Biopsy shows foamy CD68-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes.
qx.q: Which molecular finding most often guides targeted therapy?
opts: BCR-ABL fusion
JAK2 V617F alone
BRAF V600E mutation, treated with a BRAF inhibitor such as vemurafenib
IDH1 R132H mutation
MYD88 L265P mutation
qx.why: Roughly half of patients have BRAF V600E, and BRAF inhibitors produce durable responses including in CNS disease; MEK inhibitors suit BRAF-wild-type cases with MAPK pathway alterations. The other mutations belong to CML, myeloproliferative neoplasms, glioma and Waldenström macroglobulinaemia respectively.

name: Ergocalciferol (vitamin D) deficiency
formal: Vitamin D deficiency leading to rickets or osteomalacia, with proximal myopathy, bone pain, hypocalcaemic seizures or tetany and, in some reports, other neurological symptoms.
simple: Too little vitamin D, which can weaken bones and muscles and lower calcium in the blood.
th: ภาวะขาดวิตามินดี ทำให้กระดูกอ่อน (rickets/osteomalacia) กล้ามเนื้อต้นแขนขาอ่อนแรง ปวดกระดูก และแคลเซียมต่ำจนชักหรือเกร็งได้
tempoNote: Weakness and bone pain develop over months; hypocalcaemic seizures or tetany can be acute
feat: Proximal weakness with waddling gait and difficulty rising from a chair; CK usually normal
Diffuse bone pain and tenderness, pseudofractures; in children bowed legs and delayed walking
Hypocalcaemia: perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm, Chvostek and Trousseau signs, seizures in infants
Risk factors: little sun, covered skin, dark skin, malabsorption, liver/kidney disease, enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs, obesity
Reflexes preserved or brisk, unlike neuropathy
inv: 25-hydroxyvitamin D (deficiency usually < 20 ng/mL), calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, PTH
Magnesium and renal function; coeliac or malabsorption screen if unexplained
X-rays for pseudofractures (Looser zones) or rachitic changes; CK and EMG if myopathy unclear

case.who: 38-year-old woman from Pattani who works indoors and wears full-coverage clothing
case.story: Eight months of aching hips and ribs and increasing trouble climbing stairs; takes carbamazepine for epilepsy.
case.exam: Waddling gait, hip flexor weakness 4/5, bone tenderness, reflexes normal.
case.tests: 25-OH vitamin D 6 ng/mL, low-normal calcium, low phosphate, high ALP and PTH; CK normal.
case.q: What causes her weakness, and how is it treated?
case.a: Osteomalacic myopathy from vitamin D deficiency (worsened by enzyme-inducing carbamazepine); replace vitamin D with calcium and review the antiseizure drug.

Chapter 16 Neurologic Dysfunction and Kidney Disease
Chapter 125: Neurologic Complications of Nutritional Disorders

det.patho: Vitamin D (ergocalciferol D2 or cholecalciferol D3) is hydroxylated in liver and kidney to active calcitriol, which drives intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption. Deficiency causes secondary hyperparathyroidism, defective bone mineralisation and low phosphate. Muscle vitamin D receptors and hypophosphataemia contribute to type 2 fibre atrophy and weakness.
det.clinical: Neuromuscular features are proximal weakness, fatigue and myalgia with bone pain. Infants and young children may present with hypocalcaemic seizures or tetany. Severe deficiency can mimic myopathy or even motor neuron disease, and is underrecognised in elderly, housebound and veiled patients. It is a non-neurological disease with neuromuscular consequences.
det.diagnosis: Measure 25-hydroxyvitamin D with calcium, phosphate, ALP and PTH. Myopathy is usually diagnosed clinically with normal CK; EMG may be normal or mildly myopathic. Look for an underlying cause such as malabsorption, renal disease or medication.
det.treatment: Replace vitamin D (e.g. cholecalciferol 50,000 IU weekly for 8 weeks or daily equivalent, then maintenance) with adequate calcium. Treat symptomatic hypocalcaemia with IV calcium gluconate and correct magnesium. Use active vitamin D analogues in renal failure or hypoparathyroidism. Muscle strength usually improves over weeks to months.
det.prognosis: Weakness and bone pain usually recover fully with replacement.
pearls: Proximal weakness + bone pain + high ALP with normal CK: check vitamin D.
Enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs accelerate vitamin D breakdown.
Hypocalcaemic seizures in an infant: check vitamin D and maternal status.
det.thd: ภาวะขาดวิตามินดีทำให้กระดูกสะสมแร่ธาตุไม่ดี (osteomalacia ในผู้ใหญ่ และ rickets ในเด็ก) ผู้ป่วยปวดกระดูก กล้ามเนื้อต้นขาและสะโพกอ่อนแรง เดินแบบเป็ด ค่า CK มักปกติ ขณะที่ ALP และ PTH สูง เด็กเล็กอาจชักหรือเกร็งจากแคลเซียมต่ำ พบบ่อยในผู้ที่ไม่ค่อยโดนแดดหรือกินยากันชักกลุ่มเหนี่ยวนำเอนไซม์ รักษาด้วยการเสริมวิตามินดีร่วมกับแคลเซียม อาการมักดีขึ้นทั้งหมด

name: Ergot poisoning
formal: Ergotism from ergot alkaloids or overuse of ergotamine, causing severe vasoconstriction, limb ischaemia, headache, seizures and cerebral vasospasm or stroke.
simple: Poisoning from a fungus on grain or too much of an ergot migraine drug, narrowing blood vessels and causing pain, cramps or stroke.
th: พิษจาก ergot alkaloid หรือใช้ ergotamine เกินขนาด ทำให้หลอดเลือดหดตัวรุนแรง แขนขาขาดเลือด ปวดศีรษะ ชัก และหลอดเลือดสมองหดตัว
tempoNote: Acute after overdose or drug interaction; subacute with chronic overuse
feat: Cold, pale, painful limbs with weak pulses from arterial vasospasm
Headache, confusion, seizures, and occasionally stroke from cerebral vasoconstriction
Classic trigger: ergotamine combined with CYP3A4 inhibitors (HIV protease inhibitors, macrolides, azole antifungals)
Nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain from mesenteric ischaemia
Historical convulsive ergotism from contaminated rye with hallucinations and seizures
inv: Medication history including over-the-counter Cafergot-type tablets
Arterial Doppler or angiography: smooth, diffuse tapering of limb arteries
CT/MR angiography for cerebral vasoconstriction; MRI for infarcts
Renal function and CK if limb ischaemia is severe

case.who: 34-year-old man from Chiang Mai on ritonavir-boosted HIV treatment
case.story: Bought ergotamine-caffeine tablets for migraine; two days later both feet became cold and painful and he developed confusion.
case.exam: Pale cool feet with absent dorsalis pedis pulses, drowsy, mild left-sided weakness.
case.tests: Angiography shows diffuse smooth narrowing of femoral arteries; MRI shows a small right frontal infarct.
case.q: What interaction caused this?
case.a: Ritonavir inhibited CYP3A4, raising ergotamine levels and causing ergotism with limb and cerebral vasospasm.

det.patho: Ergot alkaloids act on alpha-adrenergic, serotonin and dopamine receptors, producing intense and prolonged vasoconstriction. Toxicity follows overdose, chronic overuse or inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism. Prolonged spasm leads to tissue ischaemia, thrombosis and gangrene; cerebral vessels can also be affected.
det.clinical: Gangrenous ergotism presents with burning limb pain, pallor and later gangrene. Convulsive ergotism, historically from fungal-contaminated grain, causes seizures, hallucinations and myoclonus. Modern cases usually arise from ergotamine for migraine combined with interacting drugs. Neurological features include headache, encephalopathy, seizures and ischaemic stroke.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis rests on exposure history and evidence of diffuse arterial vasospasm on imaging. A full medication history, including HIV and antifungal drugs and over-the-counter combination products, is essential. Exclude embolism, vasculitis and RCVS from other triggers.
det.treatment: Stop the ergot and the interacting drug immediately. Vasodilators such as intravenous nitroprusside, nitroglycerin, calcium channel blockers or prostacyclin analogues are used for limb ischaemia; heparin may prevent secondary thrombosis. Seizures are treated with benzodiazepines. Surgical debridement or amputation may be needed for gangrene.
det.prognosis: Usually reversible if recognised early; delayed treatment risks limb loss and permanent brain injury.
pearls: Ergotamine plus a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is a dangerous combination.
Bilateral cold limbs with smooth arterial tapering in a migraineur: ask about ergot use.
Triptans and ergots should not be combined within 24 hours.
det.thd: Ergot poisoning หรือ ergotism เกิดจากยา ergotamine เกินขนาดหรือใช้ร่วมกับยาที่ยับยั้ง CYP3A4 เช่น ritonavir, clarithromycin, ketoconazole ทำให้หลอดเลือดหดตัวรุนแรง แขนขาเย็นซีดและปวด อาจขาดเลือดถึงขั้นเนื้อตาย และมีอาการทางสมอง เช่น สับสน ชัก stroke การรักษาคือหยุดยาทันทีและให้ยาขยายหลอดเลือด

name: Essential myoclonus
formal: Idiopathic or familial disorder of non-epileptic myoclonic jerks without other neurological signs, often alcohol-responsive, and frequently overlapping with myoclonus-dystonia due to SGCE mutations.
simple: A condition of sudden muscle jerks with no other illness, which sometimes runs in families and may improve with alcohol.
th: ภาวะกระตุกแบบไม่ใช่ลมชักที่ไม่ทราบสาเหตุหรือถ่ายทอดทางพันธุกรรม ไม่มีอาการทางระบบประสาทอื่น มักดีขึ้นเมื่อดื่มแอลกอฮอล์
tempoNote: Begins in childhood or adolescence, then stable or slowly changing through adult life
feat: Brief 'lightning' jerks of neck, trunk and arms, at rest and with action
No seizures, no ataxia and no cognitive decline
Often alcohol-responsive; family history in many (autosomal dominant)
Mild dystonia (cervical or writer's cramp) suggests myoclonus-dystonia due to SGCE
Psychiatric comorbidity (anxiety, OCD, depression) is common in SGCE carriers
inv: EEG normal; EMG shows subcortical-type jerks (bursts longer than cortical, no giant SEP)
MRI normal
SGCE testing (maternally imprinted — paternal inheritance expressed); exclude metabolic and drug causes

case.story: Since age 10 he has quick jerks of the neck and arms that spill drinks; a beer or two makes them almost disappear. His father has the same.
case.exam: Multifocal proximal jerks at rest and on reaching, mild right writer's cramp; otherwise normal.
case.tests: EEG normal; MRI normal; heterozygous SGCE variant inherited from the father.
case.q: What is the diagnosis, and what treatment options exist?
case.a: Myoclonus-dystonia (SGCE); clonazepam, zonisamide or levetiracetam help, and GPi deep brain stimulation is effective for disabling cases.

read.where: Chapter 18 Myoclonus: Phenomenology, etiology, physiology, and treatment

det.patho: Many familial cases carry inactivating SGCE variants (epsilon-sarcoglycan), which is maternally imprinted so disease usually follows paternal transmission. Dysfunction of cerebellar-thalamic-basal ganglia circuits is thought to generate subcortical myoclonus. Other cases are sporadic with no identified cause.
det.clinical: Onset in the first two decades with proximal jerks that worsen with action, stress or caffeine and improve with alcohol. Dystonia may be mild or the main problem. The course is benign but social impairment and alcohol misuse are risks. Psychiatric features such as anxiety and obsessive-compulsive symptoms are part of the SGCE phenotype.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis is clinical with normal EEG, MRI and examination apart from jerks and dystonia. Neurophysiology confirms non-cortical myoclonus. Genetic testing for SGCE and related genes (e.g. KCTD17) supports diagnosis; exclude Wilson disease and drug-induced myoclonus in young patients.
det.treatment: Clonazepam, zonisamide, levetiracetam, valproate or anticholinergics may help; sodium oxybate has been tried. Bilateral GPi deep brain stimulation gives substantial improvement in severe myoclonus-dystonia. Counsel about alcohol dependence.
det.prognosis: Non-progressive; life expectancy normal.
pearls: Alcohol-responsive jerks + mild dystonia from childhood: test SGCE.
Paternal transmission pattern because of maternal imprinting.
GPi-DBS works well in disabling cases.
det.thd: Essential myoclonus คือการกระตุกที่ไม่ใช่ลมชัก เริ่มตั้งแต่เด็กหรือวัยรุ่น ไม่มีอาการทางระบบประสาทอื่น หลายรายเป็นกรรมพันธุ์และตอบสนองต่อแอลกอฮอล์ ถ้ามี dystonia ร่วมด้วยให้นึกถึง myoclonus-dystonia จากยีน SGCE EEG และ MRI ปกติ รักษาด้วย clonazepam, zonisamide หรือ levetiracetam และในรายรุนแรงใช้ DBS ที่ GPi โรคไม่ลุกลาม

name: Essential palatal tremor
formal: Rhythmic, often audible clicking of the soft palate from tensor veli palatini contraction, without structural brainstem lesion, usually in younger people and often with ear clicking.
simple: A rhythmic movement of the soft palate at the back of the mouth with no clear cause, sometimes causing a clicking sound in the ear.
th: การหดตัวเป็นจังหวะของเพดานอ่อนจากกล้ามเนื้อ tensor veli palatini ทำให้ได้ยินเสียงคลิกในหู โดยไม่มีรอยโรคในก้านสมอง มักพบในคนอายุน้อย
tempoNote: Persistent; may vary with attention or sleep
feat: Rhythmic palatal movement with audible ear clicking
Usually young patients, no other neurological signs
Movements may stop during sleep and can be voluntarily influenced
Many cases are now regarded as functional or voluntary
inv: MRI brainstem (normal; no olivary hypertrophy)
Electrophysiology to assess entrainability

case.story: Clicking sounds in both ears for a year that others can sometimes hear.
case.exam: Rhythmic soft palate elevation about 2 Hz, stops when distracted, otherwise normal neurology.
case.tests: MRI brainstem normal.
case.q: How does this differ from symptomatic palatal tremor?
case.a: Symptomatic palatal tremor involves levator veli palatini with brainstem lesion and olivary hypertrophy, without ear clicking; essential form involves tensor veli palatini and normal MRI.

read.where: 18 - Myoclonus: Phenomenology, etiology, physiology, and treatment

det.patho: Contraction of tensor veli palatini opens the Eustachian tube, producing clicks. No structural lesion is found. A large proportion of cases are thought to be functional or voluntary, and a few are tics.
det.clinical: Patients complain of ear clicking. Palatal movements are visible on examination. No other neurological signs. Symptoms may fluctuate and stop with distraction or sleep.
det.diagnosis: Normal MRI brainstem and absence of olivary hypertrophy separate it from symptomatic palatal tremor. Electrophysiology can show entrainment or variability suggesting a functional cause.
det.treatment: Reassurance and explanation. Botulinum toxin to tensor veli palatini can stop clicking. Functional cases may benefit from behavioural approaches.
det.prognosis: Benign; may persist, but no progression.
pearls: Ear clicking suggests essential palatal tremor.
Normal MRI brainstem rules out symptomatic forms.
Many essential cases are functional.
det.thd: Essential palatal tremor คือเพดานอ่อนหดตัวเป็นจังหวะจากกล้ามเนื้อ tensor veli palatini ทำให้มีเสียงคลิกในหู MRI ก้านสมองปกติ พบในคนอายุน้อย และหลายรายเป็น functional ต่างจาก symptomatic palatal tremor ที่มีรอยโรคก้านสมอง รักษาด้วยการอธิบาย และฉีด botulinum toxin ถ้าเสียงคลิกรบกวนมาก

Progressive ataxia with palatal tremor and brainstem atrophy
