name: Anti-PL-12 antibody
formal: An anti-synthetase autoantibody against alanyl-tRNA synthetase; it is rare and gives a lung-dominant anti-synthetase syndrome in which ILD is frequent and often severe while myositis is mild or absent, with overlap features of systemic sclerosis such as oesophageal dysmotility, skin sclerosis and pulmonary hypertension.
simple: A rare 'anti-synthetase' antibody that mostly attacks the lungs. Muscle weakness may be slight or absent, and some patients also have features of scleroderma, such as stiff skin, heartburn and high lung pressure.
th: Anti-PL-12 เป็นแอนติบอดีต่อ alanyl-tRNA synthetase พบน้อย อาการเด่นที่ปอด ILD ซึ่งมักรุนแรง กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงน้อยหรือไม่มี และอาจมีลักษณะคล้าย systemic sclerosis
tempoNote: Usually an insidious lung course over months; weakness, if it appears at all, is mild and late
feat: ILD-predominant presentation, frequently labelled idiopathic NSIP or UIP before serology is checked
Myositis often mild, subclinical or absent; CK normal or modestly raised
Scleroderma overlap: sclerodactyly, reflux and oesophageal dysmotility, Raynaud phenomenon, pulmonary hypertension
Mechanic's hands, arthralgia and skin lesions are possible but less consistent
inv: Extended myositis panel; PL-12 is often accompanied by Ro52
HRCT, lung function with DLCO, echocardiogram for pulmonary hypertension
Barium swallow or manometry if dysphagia or reflux; nailfold capillaroscopy for scleroderma pattern
CK and muscle MRI to detect subclinical myositis

case.who: 58-year-old woman, market vendor from Nakhon Pathom
case.story: A year of slowly increasing breathlessness diagnosed as 'idiopathic lung fibrosis', with heartburn, food sticking behind the sternum and blue fingertips in air-conditioned rooms; she denies weakness.
case.exam: Tight shiny skin over the fingers, nailfold dilated capillaries, bibasal crackles; muscle strength 5/5 throughout.
case.tests: CK 190 U/L; PL-12 and Ro52 positive; HRCT fibrotic NSIP; estimated pulmonary artery pressure raised on echocardiography.
case.q: Is this a myositis antibody without myositis — and does that matter?
case.a: Yes: PL-12 often presents as ILD with scleroderma overlap and little muscle disease. Recognising it shifts care from antifibrotic-only treatment to immunosuppression (plus antifibrotic if progressive) and prompts screening for pulmonary hypertension.

det.patho: Alanyl-tRNA synthetase charges tRNA with alanine. Like other synthetase antibodies, anti-PL-12 is thought to arise from a lung-centred immune response, and in this subtype the lung and vascular features clearly outweigh the muscle.
det.clinical: Fewer than 2 % of myositis patients carry PL-12. Most present with progressive ILD, often with features borrowed from systemic sclerosis: skin sclerosis of the fingers, oesophageal involvement and pulmonary hypertension. Myositis is frequently mild or found only on imaging, and many patients never meet classic myositis criteria. ILD is the main cause of death.
det.diagnosis: Send an extended myositis panel in any 'idiopathic' ILD, especially with Raynaud, reflux or abnormal nailfold capillaries. Confirm a weak band if the picture is atypical. Work-up includes HRCT, lung function, echocardiography, oesophageal studies and muscle imaging even when strength is normal.
det.treatment: Immunosuppression as for myositis-associated ILD: glucocorticoids with mycophenolate or tacrolimus, then rituximab or cyclophosphamide for progression. Nintedanib is added for progressive fibrosis; pulmonary hypertension is managed with specialist vasodilator therapy. Proton-pump inhibitors and dietary measures help oesophageal symptoms.
det.prognosis: Generally worse than Jo-1 disease because ILD is more severe and recognised late; pulmonary hypertension further shortens survival. Muscle outcome is rarely the problem.
pearls: PL-12 = lungs first, muscles last (or never).
Scleroderma features plus ILD with a synthetase band: think PL-12.
Normal strength does not mean this is not a myositis-spectrum disease.
det.thd: Anti-PL-12 พบน้อยมากในผู้ป่วยกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ อาการเด่นคือโรคปอด ILD ที่รุนแรงและมักถูกวินิจฉัยเป็นพังผืดในปอดไม่ทราบสาเหตุ กล้ามเนื้ออาจอ่อนแรงน้อยหรือไม่มีเลย บางรายมีลักษณะซ้อนกับ systemic sclerosis เช่น ผิวนิ้วตึง กรดไหลย้อน กลืนลำบาก และความดันหลอดเลือดปอดสูง ควรส่ง myositis panel ในผู้ป่วย ILD ทุกรายที่หาสาเหตุไม่ได้

name: Rare anti-synthetase antibodies (EJ, OJ, KS, Zo, Ha)
formal: Uncommon anti-aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase autoantibodies — anti-EJ (glycyl), anti-OJ (isoleucyl), anti-KS (asparaginyl), anti-Zo (phenylalanyl) and anti-Ha (tyrosyl) — each present in a small percentage of myositis patients and each producing a variant of the anti-synthetase syndrome with its own balance of lung, muscle, joint and skin disease.
simple: A group of rare 'anti-synthetase' antibodies. They cause the same kind of disease as Jo-1 (lungs, muscles, joints, skin), but each one tips the balance a bit differently, and doctors have less data about them.
th: กลุ่มแอนติบอดี anti-synthetase ที่พบน้อย ได้แก่ EJ, OJ, KS, Zo และ Ha ทำให้เกิด anti-synthetase syndrome เช่นเดียวกับ Jo-1 แต่สัดส่วนอาการปอด กล้ามเนื้อ ข้อ และผิวหนังต่างกันในแต่ละชนิด
tempoNote: Course mirrors other synthetase syndromes: weeks to months, often with lung disease leading; KS- and OJ-related ILD can be slowly fibrotic
feat: Anti-EJ: prominent myositis and frequent DM-like skin lesions, with ILD
Anti-OJ: ILD and myositis, but arthritis is uncommon; may be missed by some line blots
Anti-KS: lung-dominant disease, sometimes severe ILD with little or no myositis
Anti-Zo and anti-Ha: very rare, known mostly from case reports; phenotype not well defined
inv: Extended myositis immunoblot; consider immunoprecipitation at a reference laboratory when the clinical picture is strongly suggestive but the blot is unclear
HRCT and lung function with DLCO in every case
CK, aldolase and muscle MRI; biopsy showing perifascicular necrosis supports an anti-synthetase myopathy
Echocardiogram if breathlessness exceeds the extent of ILD

case.story: Eighteen months of slowly worsening exertional dyspnoea labelled 'chronic lung disease', now with thigh weakness for two months; no joint pain.
case.exam: Bibasal crackles, mild cracking of the lateral finger pads, hip flexor weakness 4/5; no rash, no synovitis.
case.tests: CK 1,900 U/L; standard blot negative for Jo-1, PL-7 and PL-12 but positive for OJ; HRCT fibrotic NSIP; MRI shows thigh oedema.
case.q: What does the OJ result explain, and why might it be missed?
case.a: An OJ anti-synthetase syndrome: ILD plus myositis with characteristically little arthritis. OJ is hard to detect on some commercial assays, so a negative 'synthetase screen' should be questioned when the phenotype fits.

det.patho: Each antibody targets a different cytoplasmic enzyme that loads a specific amino acid onto its tRNA. Usually only one synthetase antibody is present in a given patient. Why different enzymes produce slightly different organ patterns is not understood.
det.clinical: Individually these antibodies occur in roughly 1-5 % of myositis cohorts or less, so data are limited and should be read cautiously. EJ tends to give myopathy and skin lesions; OJ gives ILD and myositis with little arthritis; KS has been linked with severe ILD; Zo and Ha are described only in small series. All may present first through the lung.
det.diagnosis: Commercial assays vary in which rare synthetases they include and how reliably they detect them (OJ in particular). When a typical synthetase phenotype has a negative blot, ask for immunoprecipitation or a second method. Every positive patient needs full lung assessment.
det.treatment: Treatment is the same as for other anti-synthetase syndromes and is driven by ILD severity: glucocorticoids plus mycophenolate, azathioprine or tacrolimus, rituximab or cyclophosphamide for refractory disease, and antifibrotic therapy for progressive fibrosis.
det.prognosis: Non-Jo-1 synthetase syndromes overall have worse survival than Jo-1, mostly from lung fibrosis and pulmonary hypertension; long-standing disease carries the highest risk.
pearls: EJ = muscle and skin; OJ = no arthritis; KS = lungs.
A synthetase-shaped patient with a blank blot may still have OJ — use a second method.
Zo and Ha: report, refer and record — the phenotype is still being written.
det.thd: กลุ่ม anti-synthetase ที่พบน้อย ได้แก่ EJ, OJ, KS, Zo และ Ha แต่ละชนิดพบไม่เกินไม่กี่เปอร์เซ็นต์ EJ มักมีกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบและผื่น OJ มักไม่มีข้ออักเสบ KS มักมีโรคปอดรุนแรง ส่วน Zo และ Ha มีรายงานน้อยมาก ชุดตรวจบางชนิดอาจตรวจไม่พบโดยเฉพาะ OJ หากอาการเข้าได้แต่ผลลบควรส่งตรวจยืนยันวิธีอื่น การรักษาเหมือน anti-synthetase syndrome ทั่วไปโดยพิจารณาจากความรุนแรงของปอด

name: Anti-MDA5 antibody
formal: A dermatomyositis-specific autoantibody against melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (IFIH1), a cytoplasmic RNA sensor of innate antiviral immunity; it marks clinically amyopathic or hypomyopathic dermatomyositis with distinctive skin ulceration and palmar papules and, especially in East Asian patients, rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease with high early mortality.
simple: A blood antibody seen in a type of dermatomyositis where muscles are only slightly weak or not weak at all, the skin can ulcerate, and the lungs can get worse very fast. It is an emergency in many Asian patients.
th: Anti-MDA5 เป็นแอนติบอดีจำเพาะต่อ dermatomyositis ชนิดกล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงน้อยหรือไม่มี (clinically amyopathic) มีแผลที่ผิวหนังและตุ่มที่ฝ่ามือ และในคนเอเชียมักมีโรคปอด ILD ที่ลุกลามเร็วและเสียชีวิตสูง
tempoNote: Skin changes come first over weeks; lung disease may then progress over days to a few weeks — the first 3-6 months carry most of the mortality
feat: Skin: painful ulcers over Gottron sites, elbows and finger pads, tender palmar papules, hair loss, mouth ulcers and mechanic's hands
Muscle: weakness absent or mild and CK often normal or only slightly raised (clinically amyopathic DM)
Lung: rapidly progressive ILD in many East Asian patients, often resistant to standard treatment; slower ILD in European and US cohorts
Arthritis and hand swelling may mimic rheumatoid arthritis; fever and very high ferritin signal active systemic disease
Pneumomediastinum and sudden hypoxia are warning signs of fulminant disease
inv: MDA5 antibody (line blot or ELISA); high titre and Ro52 co-positivity add risk
Urgent HRCT and lung function or oxygen saturation trend; repeat early if symptoms change
Ferritin, CRP, LDH, lymphocyte count and KL-6 as prognostic markers
Skin biopsy for interface dermatitis and vasculopathy; CK and muscle MRI for subclinical myositis

case.who: 39-year-old woman, office worker from Khon Kaen
case.story: Six weeks of painful sores on the knuckles and finger pads, small tender bumps on the palms and hair loss; over the last ten days she has become short of breath walking to the bathroom.
case.exam: Ulcerated papules over the metacarpophalangeal joints and elbows, palmar papules, faint heliotrope; SpO2 91 % on room air; strength 5/5.
case.tests: CK 160 U/L; ferritin 2,600 ng/mL; MDA5 strongly positive with Ro52; HRCT shows patchy lower-lobe consolidation and ground glass.
case.q: Why can this not wait for the next rheumatology clinic?
case.a: MDA5-positive DM with high ferritin and early lung changes risks rapidly progressive ILD. Admit and start combined therapy at once: high-dose glucocorticoid with a calcineurin inhibitor and IV cyclophosphamide, adding a JAK inhibitor, rituximab or plasma exchange if she worsens.

det.patho: MDA5 is a cytoplasmic sensor that detects viral double-stranded RNA and triggers type I interferon production. Antibodies against it accompany intense interferon signalling, vasculopathy in skin and lung, and macrophage activation reflected by high ferritin. Seasonal and geographic clustering has suggested an environmental or viral trigger, but this is unproven.
det.clinical: MDA5 is found in a large share of East Asian adult dermatomyositis and in a smaller fraction of US and European cohorts. Muscle signs are slight, so patients present to dermatology with ulcerating papules, palmar papules, hair loss, oral ulcers and swollen hands, or to the chest service with ILD. In Asian cohorts a rapidly progressive ILD may cause death from respiratory failure within months, whereas Western cohorts more often show non-fulminant ILD. Some patients have a pure skin course that responds to steroids.
det.diagnosis: Test for MDA5 in any patient with DM-type skin lesions and little muscle weakness, or with unexplained subacute ILD and hand lesions. Risk is stratified with age, ferritin, CRP, lymphopenia, oxygen requirement and the extent of HRCT change, and some centres use composite scores. Titre may fall in remission, but its value for follow-up remains debated.
det.treatment: For high-risk or progressive lung disease, current practice is early triple therapy: high-dose glucocorticoid (often pulse methylprednisolone), a calcineurin inhibitor (tacrolimus or ciclosporin) and IV cyclophosphamide. Refractory cases may receive tofacitinib or another JAK inhibitor, rituximab, IVIG or plasma exchange, and selected patients are considered for ECMO or lung transplant. Prophylaxis against Pneumocystis and monitoring for CMV are essential under this level of immunosuppression.
det.prognosis: Early mortality is high when RP-ILD develops, particularly with high ferritin and older age. Survivors of the first six months often remain in long-term remission and relapse is less frequent than in other subtypes.
pearls: Ulcers, palmar papules and a normal CK in DM: think MDA5 and check the lungs today.
Ferritin is the cheapest risk marker you can order tonight.
In MDA5, waiting to see how the lung behaves is the most dangerous plan.
det.thd: Anti-MDA5 พบใน dermatomyositis ที่กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงน้อยหรือไม่มี แต่ผิวหนังมีแผลที่ข้อนิ้ว ข้อศอก ปลายนิ้ว และตุ่มเจ็บที่ฝ่ามือ ในผู้ป่วยชาวเอเชียรวมถึงไทยมักพบโรคปอด ILD ที่ลุกลามเร็วและเสียชีวิตสูงในช่วง 3-6 เดือนแรก ค่า ferritin สูง อายุมาก และ Ro52 บวก บ่งชี้ความเสี่ยง ควรรับไว้ในโรงพยาบาลและเริ่มการรักษาแบบสามขนาน คือสเตียรอยด์ขนาดสูง tacrolimus และ cyclophosphamide ทางหลอดเลือดโดยเร็ว

Also starts as amyopathic DM, but myositis usually follows within months and ILD is uncommon
Extensive DM skin disease in an adult, but cancer is the main threat and ILD is rare

name: Anti-TIF1-gamma antibody
formal: A dermatomyositis-specific autoantibody against transcriptional intermediary factor 1-gamma (TRIM33), formerly called anti-p155/140; in adults it is the antibody most strongly linked with cancer-associated dermatomyositis, with extensive skin disease, dysphagia and relatively low rates of ILD, whereas in juvenile DM it carries no excess cancer risk.
simple: A blood antibody in dermatomyositis that, in adults, is a strong warning sign for a hidden cancer. The skin rash is usually widespread, muscles may be only mildly weak, and the lungs are usually spared.
th: Anti-TIF1-gamma เป็นแอนติบอดีจำเพาะต่อ dermatomyositis ในผู้ใหญ่สัมพันธ์กับมะเร็งมากที่สุด ผื่นกว้างและคัน กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงไม่มาก ปอดมักไม่เป็น ส่วนในเด็กไม่เพิ่มความเสี่ยงมะเร็ง
tempoNote: Rash and weakness develop over weeks to months; the cancer is usually found within three years of onset, often already advanced
feat: Adults over about 40: high rate of associated cancer (ovary, breast, lung, gastrointestinal and, in Asia, nasopharynx)
Skin: extensive, itchy, photo-distributed rash; V-sign, shawl sign, 'red-on-white' patches, psoriasis-like or hyperkeratotic lesions
Muscle: weakness and CK often moderate; dysphagia from pharyngeal weakness is common and can be severe
Low rates of ILD, Raynaud phenomenon and calcinosis
Juvenile DM: one of the commonest antibodies, chronic skin course, no cancer link
inv: Myositis antibody panel; TIF1-gamma is best detected by ELISA or immunoprecipitation, line blots can miss weak positives

IMACS 2023 high-risk cancer screening: CT neck-chest-abdomen-pelvis, plus age- and sex-specific tests (mammography, pelvic ultrasound, CA-125, faecal or endoscopic GI screening, PSA); add PET-CT if initial tests are negative and suspicion stays high
Nasopharyngeal examination with EBV serology in Southeast Asian patients
Swallow assessment (videofluoroscopy) and CK, muscle MRI

case.who: 56-year-old woman, shop owner from Hat Yai
case.story: Three months of a burning, itchy red rash on the face, upper chest and back, and in the last month difficulty swallowing rice and coughing on water; mild difficulty rising from a low stool.
case.exam: Heliotrope rash, V-sign and shawl sign with scratch marks, Gottron papules; neck flexor 4-/5, hip flexor 4/5; nasal regurgitation on swallowing.
case.tests: CK 1,100 U/L; TIF1-gamma strongly positive; HRCT lungs normal; CT abdomen-pelvis shows a 7 cm complex left ovarian mass with raised CA-125.
case.q: What does the antibody imply for her work-up and follow-up?
case.a: TIF1-gamma DM in an adult is a high-risk cancer phenotype: full screening at diagnosis, treat the cancer (often improving the myositis), and repeat screening yearly for at least three years if the first search is negative.

det.patho: TIF1-gamma (TRIM33) is a nuclear protein that regulates transcription and TGF-beta/SMAD signalling and acts as a tumour suppressor. One model proposes that mutated or overexpressed TIF1 proteins in a tumour trigger an anti-tumour immune response that cross-reacts with regenerating muscle and skin, which would explain the close link between cancer and myositis onset.
det.clinical: The antibody is present in roughly a fifth to a third of adult DM and a similar fraction of juvenile DM. Adult patients typically have widespread, itchy skin disease, modest weakness and frequent dysphagia, while ILD and Raynaud are uncommon. Up to about half of adults, especially over 40, have a cancer; patients under 40 tend toward an amyopathic skin-dominant course with lower cancer risk. Cancers are often advanced when discovered.
det.diagnosis: The IMACS 2023 guideline places TIF1-gamma positivity (with NXP2, older age, DM subtype, dysphagia and refractory disease) in the high-risk category: enhanced screening at diagnosis, then yearly for three years. Sensitivity of line blots is imperfect, so a negative result does not exclude the antibody when the phenotype is typical.
det.treatment: Treat the cancer when found; myositis often improves after successful oncological treatment. Glucocorticoids with methotrexate, mycophenolate or azathioprine are used, and IVIG is particularly helpful for skin disease and dysphagia. Severe dysphagia may need temporary nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding.
det.prognosis: Outcome depends mostly on the cancer stage and on whether it can be treated. Without cancer, the skin disease can be chronic and troublesome but muscle prognosis is good. Juvenile TIF1-gamma DM is chronic but not malignant.
pearls: Adult + TIF1-gamma = look for cancer now, then every year for three years.
Itchy, extensive rash with dysphagia and a normal chest CT: classic TIF1-gamma pattern.
In Southeast Asia, remember the nasopharynx.
det.thd: Anti-TIF1-gamma เป็นแอนติบอดีใน dermatomyositis ที่สัมพันธ์กับมะเร็งมากที่สุดในผู้ใหญ่ โดยเฉพาะอายุมากกว่า 40 ปี ผื่นมักกว้างและคันมาก กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงปานกลาง กลืนลำบากพบบ่อย ปอดมักไม่เป็น ตามแนวทาง IMACS 2023 ผู้ป่วยกลุ่มนี้จัดเป็นความเสี่ยงสูง ควรตรวจคัดกรองมะเร็งอย่างละเอียดตั้งแต่วินิจฉัยและซ้ำทุกปีอย่างน้อย 3 ปี ในคนไทยควรตรวจโพรงหลังจมูกด้วย ส่วนในเด็กไม่สัมพันธ์กับมะเร็ง

Also florid rash, but very high CK and lower cancer risk
Umbrella for cancer-linked myositis and paraneoplastic myopathy; TIF1-gamma is its strongest serological marker

name: Anti-NXP2 antibody
formal: A dermatomyositis-specific autoantibody against nuclear matrix protein 2 (MORC3), originally described as anti-MJ; it is associated with calcinosis and contractures in juvenile DM and, in adults, with severe proximal and distal weakness, dysphagia, myalgia, subcutaneous oedema and an increased risk of cancer.
simple: A blood antibody in dermatomyositis. In children it is linked to hard calcium lumps under the skin; in adults it gives strong muscle weakness, swelling under the skin and trouble swallowing, and it raises the chance of a hidden cancer.
th: Anti-NXP2 เป็นแอนติบอดีจำเพาะต่อ dermatomyositis ในเด็กสัมพันธ์กับหินปูนใต้ผิวหนัง (calcinosis) ในผู้ใหญ่ทำให้กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงมาก กลืนลำบาก บวมใต้ผิวหนัง และเพิ่มความเสี่ยงมะเร็ง
tempoNote: Weakness, muscle pain and swelling build over weeks; calcinosis appears months to years later, especially in young children
feat: Juvenile DM: calcinosis cutis (higher risk at younger onset) and joint contractures
Adults: marked weakness including distal muscles, myalgia, dysphagia and subcutaneous or peripheral oedema
Skin rash may be mild or absent at onset, so the disease can look like polymyositis or IMNM
Cancer association in adults (male predominance in some series), weaker than TIF1-gamma
ILD uncommon
inv: Myositis antibody panel; confirm weak NXP2 bands when the phenotype is atypical
CK, muscle MRI (oedema, fascial and subcutaneous signal) and biopsy with MxA staining
Adult cancer screening per IMACS 2023 high-risk group (CT chest-abdomen-pelvis plus age-specific tests, repeated yearly)
Plain radiographs or ultrasound for calcinosis in children; swallow study if dysphagia

case.who: 8-year-old boy from Udon Thani, brought by his grandmother
case.story: One year after a diagnosis of dermatomyositis treated with prednisolone alone, he has developed hard, painful lumps at the elbows and knees, one of which discharged chalky white material.
case.exam: Faint Gottron papules, firm subcutaneous nodules at both elbows and the left knee, mild elbow flexion contractures; proximal strength 4+/5.
case.tests: CK 380 U/L; NXP2 positive; radiographs show subcutaneous calcium deposits around the elbows.
case.q: What does NXP2 explain, and what treatment lesson does this case teach?
case.a: NXP2-positive juvenile DM carries a high risk of calcinosis, particularly when disease activity is under-controlled. Early, sufficient immunosuppression (methotrexate plus steroid, IVIG if needed) is the best prevention; cancer screening is not required in children.

det.patho: NXP2 (MORC3) is a nuclear protein involved in transcription regulation and p53 activation. The antibody marks an interferon-driven dermatomyositis with prominent microvascular injury, which may underlie the oedema, calcinosis and ulceration seen in some patients.
det.clinical: NXP2 is among the commonest antibodies in juvenile DM, about a fifth to a quarter of cases, and is found in a minority of adult DM. Children develop calcinosis, especially when onset is early, and contractures. Adults often have severe weakness with distal involvement, dysphagia, myalgia and oedema, and may have little rash, so the diagnosis may be missed. Malignancy has been reported in about a third of adult patients in some cohorts, with an excess in men.
det.diagnosis: Consider NXP2 when DM or apparently rash-free myositis comes with oedema, calcinosis or striking dysphagia. Muscle biopsy showing perifascicular features and MxA staining confirms a DM pathology even without skin signs. Adults are screened for cancer as a high-risk group.
det.treatment: Glucocorticoids with methotrexate or another steroid-sparing agent; IVIG for severe weakness or dysphagia. Calcinosis is difficult to reverse — options include intensifying immunosuppression, bisphosphonates, topical or IV sodium thiosulfate and surgical removal of troublesome deposits.
det.prognosis: Muscle disease usually improves with adequate therapy, but calcinosis and contractures can cause lasting disability in children. In adults, survival is shaped by any associated cancer and by dysphagia-related aspiration.
pearls: NXP2 in a child: think calcinosis; in an adult: think cancer and swallowing.
Swollen, weak, painful limbs with little rash can still be dermatomyositis.
Calcinosis is easier to prevent with early disease control than to treat.
det.thd: Anti-NXP2 พบบ่อยใน dermatomyositis ในเด็ก และสัมพันธ์กับหินปูนใต้ผิวหนังและข้อติด โดยเฉพาะเมื่อเริ่มป่วยอายุน้อยและควบคุมโรคได้ไม่ดี ในผู้ใหญ่ทำให้กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงมากรวมถึงส่วนปลาย ปวดกล้ามเนื้อ บวมใต้ผิวหนัง และกลืนลำบาก ผื่นอาจไม่ชัดจึงวินิจฉัยช้า ผู้ใหญ่ควรตรวจคัดกรองมะเร็งแบบกลุ่มเสี่ยงสูง ส่วนเด็กไม่จำเป็น

Rash-free NXP2 disease with severe weakness can mimic necrotising myopathy; SRP has necrosis without DM pathology
Very high CK and necrosis without perifascicular change, MxA staining or DM skin signs

name: Anti-SAE antibody
formal: A rare dermatomyositis-specific autoantibody against small ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme (SAE1/SAE2); patients typically present with prominent skin disease and little weakness, then often develop myositis within months, with frequent dysphagia, uncommon ILD and a possible modest cancer association.
simple: A rare blood antibody in dermatomyositis. The rash comes first and is often hard to control; muscle weakness and trouble swallowing usually follow a few months later. The lungs are usually less affected.
ab: small ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme antibody
th: Anti-SAE เป็นแอนติบอดีที่พบน้อยใน dermatomyositis ผื่นเด่นมาก่อน กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงมักตามมาภายในไม่กี่เดือน กลืนลำบากพบบ่อย โรคปอดพบไม่บ่อย
tempoNote: Rash first, often for months; myositis and dysphagia frequently follow within weeks to months
feat: Skin-predominant onset: classic DM rash that may be extensive and resistant to treatment
Initially amyopathic or mildly myopathic, but clinically evident myositis usually emerges with time
Dysphagia is notably frequent
ILD uncommon and usually mild in Western cohorts, more frequent in Asian reports
Possible cancer association — screening still advised in adults
inv: Myositis antibody panel; isolated low-level SAE bands need clinical correlation
CK and muscle MRI at baseline and repeated if weakness appears
Swallow assessment; baseline HRCT and lung function
Age-appropriate cancer screening (IMACS 2023 risk assessment)

case.who: 61-year-old man, retired civil servant from Nakhon Ratchasima
case.story: Five months of a violaceous rash on the eyelids, neck and knuckles treated as eczema; for three weeks he has coughed when drinking and found his arms tired when combing his hair.
case.exam: Heliotrope rash, V-sign, Gottron papules; deltoid and neck flexor 4/5; wet voice after a sip of water.
case.tests: CK 640 U/L (normal two months ago); SAE positive; HRCT clear; videofluoroscopy shows pharyngeal residue and penetration.
case.q: What course does this antibody predict, and what is the immediate safety issue?
case.a: SAE DM: skin first, myositis later, with prominent dysphagia. The priority is swallowing safety (diet modification, possibly IVIG) alongside immunosuppression and age-appropriate cancer screening.

det.patho: SAE activates SUMO, a small protein attached to other proteins to alter their function (sumoylation). The antibody marks a dermatomyositis subset, with an HLA class II association reported in UK patients; the mechanism linking the antigen to disease is not established.
det.clinical: SAE is uncommon, found in a few percent of European DM and less in North American cohorts, with HLA and ethnic variation. Almost all patients have cutaneous disease, often the typical DM rash, and many initially look amyopathic before weakness appears. Dysphagia is more common than in SAE-negative DM. ILD is infrequent and usually mild outside Asia.
det.diagnosis: Consider repeat CK and muscle assessment in an SAE-positive patient labelled amyopathic, because myositis often follows. Baseline lung imaging and swallow assessment are sensible, and adults are screened for cancer according to their overall risk.
det.treatment: Glucocorticoids with methotrexate, mycophenolate or azathioprine; IVIG for refractory skin disease or dysphagia; hydroxychloroquine and topical therapy plus strict sun protection for the skin. Skin disease may need several treatment changes.
det.prognosis: Generally favourable for muscle and survival, but the skin can be stubborn and dysphagia must be managed to avoid aspiration.
pearls: SAE: the rash arrives first, the muscles catch up.
Ask about swallowing at every visit.
'Amyopathic' at diagnosis is often temporary in SAE disease — re-check CK.
det.thd: Anti-SAE พบน้อยใน dermatomyositis ผู้ป่วยมักมีผื่นเด่นก่อนโดยกล้ามเนื้อยังไม่อ่อนแรง และต่อมาภายในไม่กี่เดือนมักมีกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบชัดเจน กลืนลำบากพบบ่อยจึงต้องประเมินการกลืนทุกครั้ง โรคปอดพบไม่บ่อย ผื่นอาจควบคุมยากต้องปรับยาหลายครั้ง แต่โดยรวมการพยากรณ์โรคดี ผู้ใหญ่ควรคัดกรองมะเร็งตามความเสี่ยง

name: Anti-SRP antibody
formal: A myositis-specific autoantibody against the signal recognition particle (mainly SRP54) that targets nascent proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum; it defines a subtype of immune-mediated necrotising myopathy with rapidly progressive severe proximal weakness, very high CK, frequent dysphagia and neck weakness, necrotic fibres with little inflammation and often refractory disease.
simple: A blood antibody that causes one of the most aggressive muscle diseases: muscles become weak quickly, muscle enzymes are extremely high, swallowing can be affected, and the disease often needs several strong drugs.
th: Anti-SRP เป็นแอนติบอดีที่ทำให้เกิด immune-mediated necrotising myopathy ชนิดรุนแรง กล้ามเนื้อต้นแขนต้นขาอ่อนแรงเร็ว CK สูงมาก กลืนลำบาก ชิ้นเนื้อพบเซลล์ตายแต่มีการอักเสบน้อย และมักดื้อต่อการรักษา
tempoNote: Weakness usually progresses over weeks to a few months and can leave the patient unable to walk; slower forms in children and some adults mimic muscular dystrophy
feat: Rapid, severe, symmetric proximal weakness, often with neck flexor and extensor involvement and early atrophy
CK typically in the many thousands, sometimes over 10,000 U/L
Dysphagia frequent; respiratory muscle and cardiac involvement possible
Rash absent; ILD occurs in a minority
Partial or poor response to glucocorticoids alone
inv: SRP antibody (line blot, ELISA or immunoprecipitation); also test HMGCR
CK, ECG, troponin I and echocardiography or cardiac MRI for myocardial involvement
Muscle MRI (widespread oedema with early fatty replacement) and biopsy: scattered necrotic and regenerating fibres, sparse lymphocytes, MHC-I and complement on sarcolemma
Spirometry including FVC (supine and erect), swallow study; HRCT if respiratory symptoms

case.who: 34-year-old woman, garment factory worker from Samut Prakan
case.story: Ten weeks of rapidly worsening weakness: she can no longer climb the factory stairs, lift her head from the pillow or swallow dry food; no rash, no statin use.
case.exam: Neck flexor 2/5, shoulder abductors and hip flexors 3/5, wasting of the thighs; reflexes reduced but present; sensation normal; no skin lesions.
case.tests: CK 14,500 U/L; SRP strongly positive, HMGCR negative; MRI shows diffuse thigh oedema with early fatty change; biopsy shows necrotic fibres with very little inflammation.
case.q: Why should treatment escalate early rather than waiting on steroids?
case.a: Anti-SRP necrotising myopathy is often steroid-refractory and causes rapid atrophy. Start glucocorticoid with IVIG and a steroid-sparing drug at once, and add rituximab early if strength and CK do not improve.

det.patho: SRP is a cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein that guides newly made proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum. The antibodies bind to the surface of muscle fibres and activate complement, producing fibre necrosis with little T-cell inflammation; titres track CK and animal transfer studies support a pathogenic role. An HLA-DR association may explain differing frequency between ethnic groups.
det.clinical: SRP is found in a few percent of myositis in European cohorts and is more common in East Asian and African-American cohorts. Patients develop rapidly progressive, disabling symmetric weakness with neck and pharyngeal involvement, very high CK and early muscle atrophy. Rash is absent. Cardiac involvement and ILD occur in a minority. Juvenile cases are rare and resemble adult disease.
det.diagnosis: ENMC criteria define IMNM by high CK, proximal weakness and necrotising pathology, with SRP or HMGCR antibodies; a typical patient with a strongly positive antibody may not need a biopsy. Cardiac screening and swallowing assessment are part of the work-up. Titre correlates with CK and activity.
det.treatment: Glucocorticoids plus early IVIG, combined with methotrexate or mycophenolate to spare steroid; rituximab is used early for refractory disease and appears particularly effective in SRP myopathy. Physiotherapy and nutritional support are essential, and long-term maintenance therapy is often needed.
det.prognosis: Among the most severe myositis subtypes, with frequent residual weakness, muscle atrophy and higher mortality when treatment is delayed or the disease is refractory.
pearls: Very high CK, no rash, can't lift the head, can't swallow: send SRP and HMGCR.
Do not let steroids alone run for months in SRP disease — escalate early.
A slowly progressive 'LGMD' with a very high CK deserves an SRP test before a genetic panel ends the search.
det.thd: Anti-SRP ทำให้เกิด immune-mediated necrotising myopathy ชนิดรุนแรง ผู้ป่วยอ่อนแรงต้นแขนต้นขาและคออย่างรวดเร็วภายในไม่กี่สัปดาห์ CK สูงมากเป็นหมื่น กลืนลำบาก และกล้ามเนื้อลีบเร็ว ไม่มีผื่น ชิ้นเนื้อพบเซลล์กล้ามเนื้อตายแต่การอักเสบน้อย มักตอบสนองไม่ดีต่อสเตียรอยด์อย่างเดียว ควรให้ IVIG และยากดภูมิร่วมตั้งแต่ต้น และใช้ rituximab เร็วถ้าไม่ดีขึ้น ควรตรวจหัวใจและการกลืนด้วย

Chronic forms of SRP myopathy can mimic LGMD; family history, genetics and absent antibody separate them
Also very high CK with necrosis, but with classic DM rash and perifascicular pathology

name: Anti-HMGCR antibody
formal: A myositis-specific autoantibody against HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis and the target of statins; it defines an immune-mediated necrotising myopathy that is strongly linked with prior statin exposure in older adults, persists or progresses after the statin is stopped, and often needs prolonged immunotherapy.
simple: A blood antibody against the same enzyme that cholesterol pills (statins) block. It can cause a serious muscle disease where muscles keep getting weaker even after the statin is stopped. Some patients never took a statin, especially younger ones.
th: Anti-HMGCR เป็นแอนติบอดีต่อเอนไซม์ HMG-CoA reductase ซึ่งเป็นเป้าหมายของยากลุ่ม statin ทำให้เกิด immune-mediated necrotising myopathy มักพบในผู้สูงอายุที่เคยได้ statin และยังอ่อนแรงต่อแม้หยุดยาแล้ว
tempoNote: Weakness develops over weeks to months, often starting months or years after a statin was begun, and continues after the statin is stopped; statin-naive young patients can have a slow, dystrophy-like course
feat: Symmetric proximal weakness with CK usually several thousand U/L
Persistence or progression despite statin withdrawal — the key difference from self-limited statin myopathy
Statin exposure common in patients over 50; younger patients often statin-naive and more treatment-resistant
Dysphagia, cardiac and lung involvement less frequent than with SRP; rash absent
Possible modest cancer association; screen according to age
inv: HMGCR antibody (ELISA is reliable and gives a titre that tracks activity)
CK serially after stopping the statin; persistent elevation beyond about 6-8 weeks prompts testing
Muscle MRI and biopsy: necrotic and regenerating fibres, sparse inflammation, sarcolemmal MHC-I and complement deposition
Age-appropriate cancer screening; lipid plan with cardiology

case.who: 68-year-old man, retired police officer from Phitsanulok
case.story: On atorvastatin for four years after a heart attack; four months of difficulty rising from a chair and lifting rice bags. The statin was stopped two months ago but he is weaker.
case.exam: Hip flexors and deltoids 3+/5, neck flexion 4/5; reflexes normal; no rash; no sensory loss.
case.tests: CK 7,200 U/L (unchanged after stopping statin); HMGCR strongly positive; MRI shows bilateral thigh oedema; HbA1c and TSH normal.
case.q: Why is this not ordinary statin myopathy, and how is his cholesterol to be managed?
case.a: Weakness and CK persisting after statin withdrawal with HMGCR antibodies indicates autoimmune necrotising myopathy needing immunotherapy (IVIG, steroids, methotrexate or rituximab). Avoid statins permanently and use non-statin lipid lowering such as a PCSK9 inhibitor or ezetimibe.

det.patho: Statins inhibit HMGCR and increase its expression in muscle; in genetically predisposed people, notably carriers of HLA-DRB1*11:01, this may break tolerance. Antibodies bind regenerating fibres and activate complement, causing necrosis with little inflammation. Titres correlate with CK and fall with clinical response, supporting a pathogenic role.
det.clinical: Most older patients have taken a statin, while a sizeable proportion overall — and most children and young adults — have not, and the strength of the statin link differs between populations. Weakness is proximal and symmetric, sometimes with neck flexor involvement, with high CK. Onset is often more insidious than SRP disease, and extramuscular features are less frequent.
det.diagnosis: Suspect it when CK stays high or weakness worsens more than about two months after stopping a statin, or in any unexplained necrotising myopathy. ENMC criteria accept a typical clinical picture plus HMGCR antibody without biopsy. Exclude hypothyroidism and drug or toxic causes.
det.treatment: IVIG is effective and may even be used as monotherapy in some patients; most receive glucocorticoids, IVIG and methotrexate or mycophenolate, with rituximab for refractory cases. Statins should be avoided for life; PCSK9 inhibitors are the usual alternative, ezetimibe or bempedoic acid case by case.
det.prognosis: Many improve, but relapse on tapering is common and long maintenance therapy is often needed. Statin-naive and younger patients tend to respond less well; titre and CK help guide tapering.
pearls: Stopped the statin and still getting weaker? Order HMGCR.
A young person with a 'dystrophy' and high CK may have treatable HMGCR myopathy.
IVIG is a first-line friend in HMGCR disease.
det.thd: Anti-HMGCR ทำให้เกิด immune-mediated necrotising myopathy มักพบในผู้สูงอายุที่ได้ยา statin มานาน ลักษณะสำคัญคือกล้ามเนื้อต้นแขนต้นขาอ่อนแรงและ CK สูงต่อเนื่องแม้หยุด statin แล้ว ต่างจาก statin myopathy ทั่วไปที่ดีขึ้นเองภายในไม่กี่สัปดาห์ บางรายโดยเฉพาะคนอายุน้อยไม่เคยได้ statin และอาจคล้ายโรคกล้ามเนื้อพันธุกรรม การรักษาใช้ IVIG สเตียรอยด์ และยากดภูมิ ห้ามใช้ statin อีกและเปลี่ยนเป็นยาลดไขมันชนิดอื่น

ddx.pt: Myalgia or mild CK rise that settles within weeks of stopping the statin; HMGCR negative
More rapid and severe, with dysphagia and cardiac involvement; no statin link
Young statin-naive HMGCR disease mimics LGMD; antibody testing prevents a misdiagnosis of dystrophy

aN: anti hmg coa reductase | hmgcr antibody | anti 200 100 | statin associated autoimmune myopathy | statin associated necrotizing myopathy | anti hmgcr myopathy | hmgcr imnm | anti hmgcr necrotising myopathy

name: Anti-cN1A antibody
formal: An autoantibody against cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase 1A (NT5C1A), the only antibody associated with sporadic inclusion body myositis; it is moderately sensitive and fairly specific among myopathies but also occurs in Sjögren syndrome and SLE, and in IBM it has been linked with more dysphagia and higher mortality.
simple: A blood antibody that supports a diagnosis of inclusion body myositis, a slow muscle disease of older people that weakens the thigh and finger muscles. A positive result is helpful but not proof, because people with Sjögren or lupus can also have it.
th: Anti-cN1A เป็นแอนติบอดีเดียวที่สัมพันธ์กับ inclusion body myositis ช่วยสนับสนุนการวินิจฉัยแต่ไม่จำเพาะทั้งหมด เพราะพบได้ใน Sjögren และ SLE ผู้ที่ผลบวกมักกลืนลำบากมากกว่า
tempoNote: IBM progresses slowly over years; diagnosis is often delayed five years or more after the first symptoms
feat: Phenotype: over 50, slowly progressive, often asymmetric weakness of finger flexors and knee extensors (quadriceps), with falls
Dysphagia common, and more frequent in cN1A-positive IBM
CK normal or mildly raised (usually below 15 times normal); no rash
Positive in roughly a third to two-thirds of IBM depending on assay
Not specific: also found in Sjögren syndrome, SLE and occasionally other myositis
inv: cN1A antibody (ELISA or cell-based assay where available)
Muscle MRI: selective involvement of deep finger flexors and anterior thigh, sparing rectus femoris
Muscle biopsy: endomysial inflammation invading non-necrotic fibres, rimmed vacuoles, protein aggregates (p62, TDP-43), mitochondrial changes
Swallow study; screen for Sjögren features and T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukaemia when appropriate

case.story: Four years of increasing trouble gripping his chisel and opening bottles, and two years of buckling knees on stairs; he has fallen three times. Treated as 'polymyositis' with prednisolone for a year without benefit.
case.exam: Weak finger flexors, worse on the left, with forearm flattening; quadriceps 3/5 left, 4/5 right; hip flexors near normal; mild dysphagia for solids.
case.tests: CK 680 U/L; cN1A positive; MRI shows deep finger flexor and vastus involvement; biopsy shows rimmed vacuoles and endomysial inflammation.
case.q: What should change in his treatment and counselling?
case.a: This is IBM: stop prolonged steroids (no benefit, more harm), arrange physiotherapy, falls prevention and swallow management, and explain the slow course. The cN1A result supports the diagnosis and alerts to dysphagia.

det.patho: cN1A hydrolyses AMP to adenosine and helps regulate nucleotide pools. IBM combines a cytotoxic T-cell attack on muscle fibres with degenerative features — rimmed vacuoles, protein aggregation; the cN1A antibody shows a humoral component as well, and passive transfer studies suggest it may contribute to protein aggregation.
det.clinical: IBM is the commonest acquired myopathy after 50. Weakness typically starts in the quadriceps or finger flexors, is often asymmetric, and progresses slowly with falls, loss of grip and dysphagia. cN1A-positive patients appear to have more oesophageal and pharyngeal problems and higher mortality after adjusting for age and comorbidity, but otherwise similar disease.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis rests on the clinical pattern with supportive biopsy (ENMC 2011 criteria). A positive cN1A helps when the biopsy lacks typical features early on, but a negative result does not exclude IBM, and positives in Sjögren syndrome and SLE limit specificity. Early, correct diagnosis spares patients ineffective steroid courses.
det.treatment: No drug has proven to slow IBM; recent trials of several agents were negative. Management is supportive: tailored exercise and physiotherapy, orthoses and walking aids, falls prevention, and swallowing therapy or cricopharyngeal procedures. IVIG may help dysphagia in selected patients. Long-term steroids are avoided.
det.prognosis: Slowly progressive disability; many need a walking aid within ten to fifteen years. Life expectancy is near normal overall, with aspiration and falls the main threats; cN1A positivity has been associated with somewhat higher mortality.
pearls: Weak grip and weak knees in an older adult: IBM until proven otherwise.
Steroid-unresponsive 'polymyositis' is often IBM.
cN1A supports, but never alone makes, the diagnosis.
det.thd: Anti-cN1A เป็นแอนติบอดีเดียวที่พบใน inclusion body myositis ซึ่งเป็นโรคกล้ามเนื้อเรื้อรังในผู้สูงอายุ ลักษณะเด่นคืออ่อนแรงของกล้ามเนื้องอนิ้วมือและต้นขาด้านหน้าแบบไม่สมมาตร ล้มบ่อย และกลืนลำบาก ผลบวกช่วยสนับสนุนการวินิจฉัยแต่ไม่จำเพาะ เพราะพบใน Sjögren และ SLE ได้ ปัจจุบันไม่มียาที่ชะลอโรคได้ การรักษาคือกายภาพบำบัด ป้องกันการล้ม และดูแลการกลืน ไม่ควรให้สเตียรอยด์ระยะยาว

ddx.pt: Rare true PM is symmetric, proximal and steroid-responsive; steroid failure in an older patient should prompt IBM review
Necrotising myopathy with higher CK and symmetric proximal weakness that responds to immunotherapy
Fatigable ptosis, diplopia and bulbar weakness with normal CK; finger flexors and quadriceps are not selectively wasted

aN: anti nt5c1a | anti mup44 | cn1a antibody | cytosolic 5 nucleotidase 1a antibody | nt5c1a antibody | ibm antibody | inclusion body myositis antibody | anti cn 1a

name: Anti-PM/Scl antibody
formal: A myositis-associated autoantibody against the PM/Scl-75 and PM/Scl-100 subunits of the nucleolar exosome complex; it marks overlap of myositis with systemic sclerosis, characterised by ILD, arthritis, mechanic's hands, Raynaud phenomenon and often subtle sclerodermatous skin change.
simple: A blood antibody that points to a 'mixed' disease: myositis plus features of scleroderma (cold colour-changing fingers, tight skin, lung scarring). The scleroderma signs can be very subtle.
th: Anti-PM/Scl เป็นแอนติบอดีที่สัมพันธ์กับกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบร่วมกับ systemic sclerosis (overlap) มีโรคปอด ILD ข้ออักเสบ มือช่าง และ Raynaud ลักษณะ scleroderma อาจไม่ชัด
tempoNote: Myositis and Raynaud usually develop over months; skin and lung changes may evolve slowly over years
feat: Myositis overlapping with systemic sclerosis or, less often, with dermatomyositis
ILD, arthritis, mechanic's hands and Raynaud phenomenon — can look like anti-synthetase syndrome
Scleroderma features may be limited to puffy fingers, telangiectasia or abnormal nailfold capillaries
Calcinosis and oesophageal dysmotility can occur; renal crisis is uncommon
inv: ANA (nucleolar pattern) and myositis/scleroderma line blot for PM/Scl-75 and -100
HRCT and lung function, echocardiogram for pulmonary hypertension
Nailfold capillaroscopy; CK and muscle MRI
Blood pressure and renal function monitoring as for scleroderma

case.story: Five months of thigh weakness and painful wrists, fingers that turn white then blue in the hospital's cold rooms, and recent breathlessness on the stairs.
case.exam: Puffy fingers, a few facial telangiectasias, cracked radial finger skin; hip flexors 4/5; bibasal crackles.
case.tests: CK 2,100 U/L; ANA nucleolar 1:640; PM/Scl-100 positive, synthetase antibodies negative; HRCT NSIP; capillaroscopy shows a scleroderma pattern.
case.q: Why is this not anti-synthetase syndrome, and what does the antibody predict?
case.a: The picture resembles ASS, but the nucleolar ANA, PM/Scl antibody and capillaroscopy point to a scleroderma-myositis overlap. Expect chronic ILD needing long-term immunosuppression; remission off treatment is uncommon.

det.patho: The PM/Scl complex is the human exosome, a nucleolar machine that degrades and processes RNA. The antibody does not itself injure muscle but marks an overlap autoimmune disease with fibrosing and vascular features of scleroderma together with inflammatory myopathy.
det.clinical: PM/Scl is among the commonest myositis-associated antibodies, enriched in patients with myositis-scleroderma overlap. Patients have myositis, arthritis, Raynaud phenomenon, mechanic's hands and ILD, and scleroderma signs may be limited to puffy fingers or a few telangiectasias, so the overlap is easily missed. The ILD can look like anti-synthetase disease on imaging.
det.diagnosis: A nucleolar ANA pattern in a patient with myositis should prompt PM/Scl testing. Look carefully for subtle scleroderma signs with capillaroscopy. Assess the lungs, heart and oesophagus at baseline as in systemic sclerosis.
det.treatment: Glucocorticoids at the lowest effective dose (high doses carry a risk of scleroderma renal crisis), combined with mycophenolate, methotrexate or azathioprine; rituximab or cyclophosphamide for progressive ILD and antifibrotic therapy for progressive fibrosis. Vasodilators manage Raynaud and digital ulcers.
det.prognosis: Survival is generally good, but the disease is chronic and complete remission off treatment is rare; ILD and pulmonary hypertension determine long-term outcome.
pearls: Nucleolar ANA + myositis = ask for PM/Scl.
Puffy fingers may be the only scleroderma clue.
Watch blood pressure and creatinine when using steroids in scleroderma overlap.
det.thd: Anti-PM/Scl เป็นแอนติบอดีที่พบบ่อยในกลุ่มกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบที่ซ้อนกับ systemic sclerosis ผู้ป่วยมีกล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรง ข้ออักเสบ Raynaud มือช่าง และโรคปอด ILD คล้าย anti-synthetase syndrome แต่ลักษณะ scleroderma อาจมีเพียงนิ้วบวมหรือเส้นเลือดฝอยขยายเล็กน้อย ANA มักเป็นแบบ nucleolar โรคมักเรื้อรังและหายขาดได้น้อย ควรใช้สเตียรอยด์ขนาดต่ำร่วมกับยากดภูมิ

ddx.pt: Same clinical cluster of ILD, arthritis and mechanic's hands, but with a synthetase antibody and no scleroderma features
Systemic sclerosis without myositis; Scl-70, centromere or RNA polymerase III antibodies
Umbrella term; PM/Scl is one of the commonest antibodies defining it, alongside U1-RNP and Ku

aN: anti pm scl | anti pmscl | pm scl antibody | pm scl 75 | pm scl 100 | anti exosome | anti pm scl 75 | anti pm scl 100 | scleromyositis antibody

name: Anti-U1-RNP antibody
formal: A myositis-associated autoantibody against the U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (70 kDa, A and C proteins); at high titre it defines mixed connective tissue disease, and in myositis it identifies an overlap form with Raynaud phenomenon, swollen hands, arthritis and a risk of ILD and pulmonary arterial hypertension, usually with good steroid responsiveness.
simple: A blood antibody that points to 'mixed connective tissue disease', a blend of lupus, scleroderma and myositis. Fingers swell and change colour in the cold, joints ache, and muscles may be weak; the muscle part usually responds well to treatment.
th: Anti-U1-RNP เป็นแอนติบอดีหลักของ mixed connective tissue disease เมื่อพบร่วมกับกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ ผู้ป่วยมี Raynaud มือบวม ข้ออักเสบ เสี่ยงต่อ ILD และความดันหลอดเลือดปอดสูง กล้ามเนื้อมักตอบสนองต่อสเตียรอยด์ดี
tempoNote: Often begins with Raynaud and puffy hands for months or years before myositis or other organ features appear
feat: Raynaud phenomenon and puffy, swollen hands are almost universal early features
Myositis usually mild to moderate and steroid-responsive
Arthritis (can be deforming), lupus-like skin and serositis, sclerodactyly
Organ risks: ILD and pulmonary arterial hypertension (the main cause of death); aseptic meningitis and trigeminal neuropathy are neurological associations
inv: ANA (speckled, high titre) and U1-RNP; check Sm, dsDNA, Scl-70 and myositis panel to define the overlap
CK, muscle MRI if weak
Echocardiogram and NT-proBNP for pulmonary hypertension; HRCT and lung function
Full blood count, urinalysis and complement for lupus features

case.story: Two years of fingers that turn white in the air-conditioned lobby and swollen hands making rings tight; three months of aching thighs, difficulty rising from a squat and painful knuckles.
case.exam: Diffusely puffy fingers, synovitis of the MCP joints, hip flexors 4/5; no rash; facial sensation normal.
case.tests: CK 1,500 U/L; ANA speckled 1:2,560; U1-RNP strongly positive, Sm and dsDNA negative; echocardiogram normal; HRCT clear.
case.q: Which complication must you screen for every year even though she feels better?
case.a: MCTD with myositis usually responds well to steroids, but pulmonary arterial hypertension and ILD drive long-term outcome — yearly echocardiography (or sooner with dyspnoea) and periodic lung function are needed.

det.patho: U1-snRNP is a spliceosome component. Apoptotic modification of the U1-70K protein is thought to expose it to the immune system, and immune complexes with its RNA stimulate innate immune receptors. The antibody marks a clinical overlap rather than causing muscle damage directly.
det.clinical: U1-RNP appears in only a few percent of adult and juvenile DM/PM but in a large share of patients with MCTD, who combine features of at least two of systemic sclerosis, myositis and SLE. Raynaud and swollen hands come early; arthritis, ILD and pulmonary arterial hypertension are the important organ risks. Trigeminal sensory neuropathy and aseptic meningitis (sometimes NSAID-related) are recognised neurological associations.
det.diagnosis: MCTD is diagnosed with high-titre U1-RNP plus a compatible overlap of clinical features. In a myositis patient, U1-RNP shifts the frame toward overlap disease and mandates screening for pulmonary hypertension and ILD.
det.treatment: Myositis and arthritis respond well to moderate-dose glucocorticoids with methotrexate, azathioprine or mycophenolate; hydroxychloroquine for lupus-like features. ILD is treated as in other CTD-ILD, and PAH with specialist vasodilator therapy, sometimes with added immunosuppression in early disease.
det.prognosis: Muscle disease carries a favourable outlook compared with other overlap antibodies such as PM/Scl. Long-term survival is set by pulmonary hypertension and ILD.
pearls: Puffy hands + Raynaud + myositis = U1-RNP; screen for PAH.
In MCTD, the muscles usually behave and the lungs decide the outcome.
Numb face in a patient with Raynaud: think trigeminal neuropathy of CTD.
det.thd: Anti-U1-RNP เป็นแอนติบอดีหลักของ mixed connective tissue disease ซึ่งเป็นโรคผสมระหว่าง lupus, scleroderma และกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ ผู้ป่วยมักเริ่มด้วย Raynaud และมือบวมมาก่อนหลายปี ต่อมามีข้ออักเสบและกล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงซึ่งมักตอบสนองต่อสเตียรอยด์ดี ภาวะแทรกซ้อนสำคัญคือความดันหลอดเลือดปอดสูงและ ILD จึงต้องตรวจ echocardiogram เป็นระยะ อาจพบ trigeminal neuropathy และ aseptic meningitis ได้

ddx.pt: The defining disease of high-titre U1-RNP; myositis is one of its components
Scleroderma-myositis overlap with nucleolar ANA; more resistant to treatment
Lupus myositis with Sm or dsDNA antibodies and renal or haematological disease

aN: anti u1 snrnp | anti rnp | u1 rnp antibody | u1 snrnp | anti u1 70k | anti nrnp | rnp antibody | mctd antibody

name: Anti-Ku antibody
formal: A myositis-associated autoantibody against the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer, a DNA-end-binding protein of double-strand break repair; it marks myositis overlapping with systemic sclerosis, SLE or Sjögren syndrome, with arthralgia, Raynaud phenomenon and ILD, where muscle disease responds to steroids but lung disease is often resistant.
simple: A blood antibody seen when myositis overlaps with lupus, scleroderma or Sjögren. The muscle part usually gets better with steroids, but the lung part can be stubborn.
th: Anti-Ku เป็นแอนติบอดีที่สัมพันธ์กับกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบซ้อนกับ SLE, scleroderma หรือ Sjögren มีปวดข้อ Raynaud และ ILD กล้ามเนื้อมักตอบสนองต่อสเตียรอยด์ แต่โรคปอดมักดื้อต่อการรักษา
tempoNote: Myositis evolves over weeks to months; ILD may develop or progress more slowly and persist after muscle remission
feat: Overlap myositis with features of SLE, systemic sclerosis or Sjögren syndrome
Arthralgia, arthritis, Raynaud phenomenon and other musculoskeletal symptoms are prominent
ILD in a subset; often steroid-resistant and outcome-defining
CK may be markedly raised; muscle biopsy can show necrotising features
inv: ANA (speckled) and Ku antibody on an extended panel; look for co-existing Ro, U1-RNP or dsDNA
HRCT and lung function at baseline and during follow-up
CK, muscle MRI and biopsy when the phenotype is unclear
Screen for Sjögren features (Schirmer test, salivary gland ultrasound) and lupus organ involvement

case.story: Four months of aching joints and thigh weakness, dry eyes and mouth, white fingers on early-morning tapping rounds, and a dry cough for six weeks.
case.exam: Mild synovitis of the wrists, hip flexors 4-/5, dry oral mucosa, fine bibasal crackles; no DM rash.
case.tests: CK 4,800 U/L; ANA speckled 1:1,280; Ku and Ro60 positive; myositis-specific antibodies negative; HRCT shows early NSIP.
case.q: What course do you expect for the muscle compared with the lung?
case.a: Ku-positive overlap myositis: the muscle typically responds to steroids, but the ILD may be steroid-resistant, so add mycophenolate early and follow lung function closely.

det.patho: Ku is a heterodimer of 70 and 80 kDa proteins that binds broken DNA ends and starts non-homologous end-joining repair. Anti-Ku antibodies are a marker of systemic overlap autoimmunity rather than a direct cause of muscle injury.
det.clinical: Ku antibodies occur in a minority of patients with overlap syndromes involving myositis with SLE, scleroderma or Sjögren syndrome. Patients often have arthralgia, Raynaud and ILD alongside myositis, which can be necrotising with high CK. Prognosis depends on the organs involved: the muscle and joints usually do well with steroids, while ILD is often refractory.
det.diagnosis: Ku antibodies are included in many extended myositis and connective tissue panels. Their presence should prompt a search for the partner connective tissue disease and baseline lung assessment, even if the patient has no respiratory complaint.
det.treatment: Glucocorticoids for muscle and joint disease, with an early steroid-sparing agent; mycophenolate, rituximab or cyclophosphamide when ILD is present or progresses. Treat the associated connective tissue disease according to its own features.
det.prognosis: Musculoskeletal disease has a good outlook; long-term outcome is driven by the presence and behaviour of ILD.
pearls: Ku: muscle listens to steroids, lungs often do not.
Myositis with dry eyes, Raynaud and a speckled ANA: ask for Ku.
Screen the lungs at diagnosis, not when the cough gets worse.
det.thd: Anti-Ku พบในผู้ป่วยกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบที่ซ้อนกับโรค SLE, scleroderma หรือ Sjögren ผู้ป่วยมักมีปวดข้อ Raynaud และอาจมี ILD กล้ามเนื้อและข้อมักตอบสนองต่อสเตียรอยด์ดี แต่โรคปอดมักดื้อต่อการรักษาและเป็นตัวกำหนดการพยากรณ์โรค จึงควรตรวจ HRCT ตั้งแต่ต้นและเริ่มยากดภูมิร่วมเร็วเมื่อพบโรคปอด

ddx.pt: Overlap with scleroderma and nucleolar ANA; ILD and mechanic's hands
Overlap with MCTD features, swollen hands and PAH risk; good steroid response
Sicca disease with Ro/La antibodies; myositis is uncommon and usually mild

aN: anti ku70 | anti ku80 | anti ku70 80 | ku antibody | anti p70 p80 | ku overlap myositis

name: Anti-Ro52 antibody (in myositis)
formal: A myositis-associated autoantibody against Ro52 (TRIM21), an intracellular E3 ubiquitin ligase and antibody receptor; it is the commonest autoantibody co-detected in myositis, frequently accompanying anti-Jo-1 and anti-MDA5, where it predicts more severe interstitial lung disease, and on its own it is non-specific.
simple: A common 'companion' antibody. Alone it means little, because it appears in many autoimmune diseases. Together with a myositis antibody such as Jo-1 or MDA5, it warns that the lungs may be hit harder.
th: Anti-Ro52 เป็นแอนติบอดีที่พบร่วมบ่อยที่สุดในโรคกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ เมื่อพบเดี่ยวไม่จำเพาะ แต่เมื่อพบร่วมกับ Jo-1 หรือ MDA5 บ่งชี้ว่าโรคปอด ILD จะรุนแรงกว่า
tempoNote: Not a disease in itself; its meaning depends on the partner antibody and the clinical course of that syndrome
feat: Found in about a third of myositis patients and many other CTDs (Sjögren, SLE, systemic sclerosis, autoimmune liver disease)
With anti-Jo-1: more mechanic's hands, more severe ILD, possibly more malignancy and worse outcome
With anti-MDA5: higher risk of rapidly progressive ILD and death
Isolated Ro52 without a myositis-specific antibody does not establish myositis
inv: Reported on most myositis and ENA line blots; check which partner antibodies are present
HRCT and lung function, with closer follow-up when combined with a synthetase or MDA5 antibody
Assess for Sjögren syndrome when Ro60/La are also positive
ECG in pregnancy planning (neonatal heart block risk with Ro antibodies)

case.story: Known anti-Jo-1 anti-synthetase syndrome for two years with stable muscles on azathioprine; now three months of worsening breathlessness and fatigue.
case.exam: Mechanic's hands, more extensive bibasal crackles than a year ago, SpO2 drops to 88 % on walking; strength 5-/5.
case.tests: CK 250 U/L; panel repeated: Jo-1 and Ro52 both strongly positive; HRCT shows progression with new reticulation; FVC fell 12 % in a year.
case.q: What does the Ro52 band add, and what should change?
case.a: Jo-1 with Ro52 carries a higher risk of severe, progressive ILD. Escalate lung-directed therapy (mycophenolate or rituximab) and add an antifibrotic if fibrosis keeps progressing.

read.where: 18: Myopathies Associated with Systemic Disorders and Aging

det.patho: Ro52 (TRIM21) is a cytoplasmic protein that binds antibody-coated viruses inside cells and tags proteins for degradation; it also regulates interferon responses. Antibodies against it arise across many interferon-driven autoimmune diseases, which explains its lack of specificity.
det.clinical: Ro52 is the most frequent autoantibody co-detected in adult myositis, roughly a third of patients, and it often co-exists with Jo-1 in the large majority of Jo-1 positive patients in some series. The combination is linked with mechanic's hands, more severe ILD and worse outcome. In MDA5-positive DM, Ro52 co-positivity is a recognised risk factor for rapidly progressive ILD. In CTD generally, Ro52 and Ro60 occur together, whereas in myositis Ro52 often appears alone.
det.diagnosis: Interpret Ro52 only alongside the rest of the panel. An isolated Ro52 band in a patient with weakness should prompt a search for an MSA, another CTD or a non-inflammatory cause rather than a myositis label. When it accompanies an MSA, use it to stratify lung risk.
det.treatment: There is no Ro52-specific treatment. It argues for closer lung monitoring and earlier escalation of immunosuppression in synthetase or MDA5 disease. Women of child-bearing age with Ro antibodies need foetal heart monitoring in pregnancy.
det.prognosis: Adds risk to the partner syndrome — especially more severe ILD — but on its own does not predict a particular course.
pearls: Ro52 alone is a passenger; with Jo-1 or MDA5 it is a warning light.
Never diagnose myositis on a Ro52 band alone.
Ro antibodies and pregnancy: think congenital heart block.
det.thd: Anti-Ro52 เป็นแอนติบอดีที่พบร่วมบ่อยที่สุดในโรคกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ ประมาณหนึ่งในสามของผู้ป่วย และพบได้ในโรคภูมิต้านตนเองอื่นอีกหลายโรค เมื่อพบเดี่ยวจึงไม่ใช้วินิจฉัยกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ แต่เมื่อพบร่วมกับ Jo-1 หรือ MDA5 บ่งชี้ว่าโรคปอด ILD จะรุนแรงและการพยากรณ์โรคแย่ลง ควรติดตามปอดใกล้ชิดและปรับยากดภูมิเร็วขึ้น หญิงวัยเจริญพันธุ์ที่มี Ro ควรเฝ้าระวังหัวใจทารกเมื่อตั้งครรภ์

name: Anti-NMDAR antibody
formal: An IgG1 autoantibody against GluN1 (NR1), the obligatory subunit of NMDA-type glutamate receptors, that cross-links and internalises synaptic receptors; detected reliably in CSF, it marks anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, a staged neuropsychiatric illness of young people that is linked to ovarian teratoma in adult women and can follow herpes simplex encephalitis.
simple: A spinal-fluid (and blood) antibody test that confirms a treatable brain inflammation of young people: odd behaviour first, then fits, abnormal mouth and limb movements, swings in pulse and blood pressure and reduced consciousness. In young women look for an ovarian tumour.
th: Anti-NMDAR เป็นแอนติบอดีต่อหน่วยย่อย GluN1 ของตัวรับ NMDA ตรวจได้ไวที่สุดในน้ำไขสันหลัง ใช้ยืนยันสมองอักเสบจากภูมิคุ้มกันชนิดที่พบบ่อยที่สุดในคนอายุน้อย สัมพันธ์กับ teratoma ของรังไข่ในหญิงวัยผู้ใหญ่ และเกิดตามหลังสมองอักเสบจากเริมได้
tempoNote: Psychiatric change evolves over days and is joined within one to three weeks by seizures, dyskinesia, autonomic storms and reduced consciousness; recovery is slow, often over 1-2 years, and about one patient in ten relapses
feat: Target and class: extracellular amino-terminal region of GluN1; mainly IgG1, complement-fixing but acting chiefly by receptor cross-linking and internalisation
Phenotype it marks: mixed psychiatric onset (mood, psychosis, catatonia, agitation), then speech loss, seizures, orofacial and limb dyskinesia, dysautonomia and central hypoventilation
Who: median age around 20, roughly four women to each man, from infancy to old age; children more often begin with seizures or movement disorder
Tumour: ovarian teratoma in about half to 60% of adult women; men, children and older adults usually have no tumour
Post-viral trigger: weeks after herpes simplex encephalitis, a fresh choreoathetoid or behavioural relapse should prompt NMDAR testing rather than repeat antivirals alone
inv: CSF and serum NMDAR-IgG by cell-based assay (ideally with tissue-based confirmation); CSF is the decisive sample because serum misses some cases and is falsely positive in a few percent of controls
CSF cell count, protein and oligoclonal bands — abnormal in most; MRI brain usually normal or non-specific
EEG: generalised slowing is common; extreme delta brush is uncommon but highly suggestive; continuous EEG if consciousness falls
Tumour search: pelvic MRI and transvaginal or transabdominal ultrasound in females; testicular ultrasound in young men if suspicious; repeat imaging if negative but relapsing

case.who: 19-year-old female university student from Khon Kaen
case.story: After a flu-like week she became suspicious of her roommates, laughed and cried without reason and stopped sleeping; a psychiatric admission followed. On day 10 she had a generalised seizure and then stopped speaking.
case.exam: Mute, staring, intermittent lip-smacking and jaw-chewing movements with dystonic hand posturing; heart rate swinging 50-140/min; no neck stiffness.
case.tests: CSF 32 lymphocytes/µL, protein normal, oligoclonal bands present; CSF NMDAR-IgG positive on cell-based assay; MRI brain normal; EEG diffuse delta slowing; pelvic MRI shows a 3 cm fat-containing right ovarian lesion.
case.q: What does the CSF antibody result change in management?
case.a: It confirms anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: remove the ovarian teratoma, give methylprednisolone with IVIG or plasma exchange at once, and escalate to rituximab (with or without cyclophosphamide) if there is no clear gain after about two weeks.

det.patho: Antibodies attach to an extracellular N-terminal region of GluN1, causing cross-linking and internalisation of NMDA receptors, reducing synaptic receptor density in a titre-dependent and reversible way, with little neuronal death. In teratoma-related disease, the tumour contains neural tissue and lymphoid follicles in which NMDAR-reactive B cells mature; after herpes simplex encephalitis, viral destruction is thought to expose receptor antigen. Antibody-secreting cells are present inside the CNS, which explains why the CSF is the more faithful sample.
det.clinical: Adults usually present to psychiatry with an abrupt, mixed syndrome that cuts across diagnostic categories — mood swings, paranoia, catatonia and insomnia — followed within days by amnesia, reduced speech, seizures and a polymorphic movement disorder dominated by orofacial dyskinesia, chorea, stereotypy and dystonia. Autonomic instability (tachy- and bradyarrhythmia, labile blood pressure, hypersalivation) and central hypoventilation often require intensive care. Children tend to start with seizures, abnormal movements or behavioural regression. Isolated psychiatric disease is seen only early in the course or in a small minority.
det.diagnosis: Send both CSF and serum. A positive CSF NMDAR-IgG on a cell-based assay in a compatible syndrome is diagnostic; serum alone can be negative in about one fifth and low-titre serum positivity occurs in healthy and disease controls, so a serum-only result without CSF support should be interpreted cautiously. Commercial fixed-cell kits are less sensitive than live-cell or tissue-based assays; if the picture is typical and the kit is negative, re-test at a reference laboratory. Graus 2016 criteria allow a diagnosis of probable NMDAR encephalitis and early treatment before results return. MRI is normal in most, CSF pleocytosis is common and EEG is abnormal in nearly all.
det.treatment: Start first-line therapy (IV methylprednisolone, usually with plasma exchange or IVIG) as soon as the syndrome is recognised, and remove a teratoma when found — removal alone is about as effective as one first-line drug. Roughly half improve within four weeks; for the rest, rituximab and/or cyclophosphamide help most patients and lower the relapse rate, so the threshold to escalate is about two weeks without clear improvement. Supportive care includes benzodiazepines for agitation and catatonia, cautious use of antipsychotics, management of dysautonomia and prolonged ICU care. Long-term maintenance agents are reserved for relapsing disease.
det.prognosis: Recovery continues for up to two years, and about four in five reach independence (mRS 0-2). Delay of immunotherapy beyond about four weeks predicts a worse outcome at one year. Relapse occurs in roughly 10-15% and is less frequent after teratoma removal and second-line therapy; mortality is around 5%. Residual problems are mostly cognitive, behavioural and sleep-related. Antibody titres fall with recovery but do not reliably track activity.
pearls: Test the CSF: it is the sample that confirms NMDAR encephalitis; serum alone misleads both ways.
Orofacial dyskinesia plus new psychiatric illness plus a swinging pulse in a young woman means pelvic imaging today.
No response to first-line treatment by two weeks is the signal to give rituximab, not to wait.
det.thd: Anti-NMDAR ควรส่งตรวจทั้งน้ำไขสันหลังและเลือด โดยผลในน้ำไขสันหลังมีน้ำหนักมากที่สุด ผู้ป่วยมักเป็นหญิงอายุน้อยที่เริ่มด้วยอาการทางจิตเวช แล้วตามด้วยชัก ไม่พูด การเคลื่อนไหวผิดปกติรอบปาก และชีพจรความดันแกว่ง ต้องตรวจหา teratoma ของรังไข่และผ่าตัดออกถ้าพบ ให้สเตียรอยด์ร่วมกับ IVIG หรือเปลี่ยนถ่ายพลาสมาโดยเร็ว และถ้าไม่ดีขึ้นใน 2 สัปดาห์ควรให้ rituximab ผู้ป่วยส่วนใหญ่ฟื้นตัวได้ดีแม้ต้องใช้เวลาหลายเดือน

name: Anti-LGI1 antibody
formal: A predominantly IgG4 autoantibody against leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1, a secreted synaptic protein that links ADAM22/ADAM23 to presynaptic Kv1 potassium channels; formerly reported as a 'VGKC-complex' antibody, it marks a limbic encephalitis of older men with faciobrachial dystonic seizures, hyponatraemia and a strong HLA-DRB1*07:01 association, usually without cancer.
simple: A blood test that explains very frequent brief jerks of the face and arm on one side in an older man, followed by memory loss and low blood sodium. It is usually not caused by cancer and responds much better to immune treatment than to seizure medicines.
th: Anti-LGI1 เป็นแอนติบอดีชนิด IgG4 ต่อโปรตีน LGI1 เดิมจัดอยู่ในกลุ่ม VGKC-complex พบในชายสูงอายุที่มีสมองอักเสบส่วน limbic ร่วมกับชักแบบ faciobrachial dystonic seizure โซเดียมต่ำ และมักไม่พบมะเร็ง
tempoNote: Faciobrachial seizures often appear weeks to months before memory decline; untreated disease may smoulder for one to several years and mimic a neurodegenerative dementia
feat: Target and class: secreted LGI1 bridging ADAM22/23 and Kv1.1; IgG4-dominant antibodies block protein-protein binding rather than fixing complement
Who: median age mid-60s, about two men per woman; more than 90% carry HLA-DRB1*07:01
Faciobrachial dystonic seizures: very brief, stereotyped, unilateral face-arm (sometimes leg) posturing, up to hundreds per day, often preceding cognitive decline
Other clues: piloerection spells, paroxysmal dizziness, fear or déjà-vu auras, ictal bradycardia, hyponatraemia in about two thirds, and dense anterograde plus autobiographical amnesia
Tumour: uncommon (well under one in ten; thymoma most often when present)
inv: Serum LGI1-IgG by cell-based assay — serum is the more sensitive sample, as CSF is negative in about half
Serum sodium (SIADH-type hyponatraemia), ECG/Holter if spells include bradycardia
MRI: medial temporal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity or swelling in about 40%, often unilateral; FBDS may show basal ganglia signal; follow-up scans can show hippocampal atrophy
EEG often normal during FBDS; CSF usually bland; chest CT for thymoma, and HLA typing as an optional adjunct in atypical cases

case.story: For two months his wife noticed his left face pulling and left arm stiffening for two seconds, 40-60 times a day, unaffected by levetiracetam. Over the last three weeks he forgot recent conversations and got lost on the way to the market.
case.exam: Frequent brief left face-arm dystonic spells; recall 0/3 at five minutes; no focal weakness.
case.tests: Serum sodium 126 mmol/L; MRI shows right hippocampal T2 hyperintensity; CSF 2 cells/µL, CSF LGI1 negative; serum LGI1-IgG positive (cell-based assay); CT chest normal.
case.q: Does the negative CSF exclude LGI1 encephalitis, and what treatment works best for the spells?
case.a: No — CSF is negative in about half, so the serum result stands. Faciobrachial dystonic seizures respond to immunotherapy (steroids, with early plasma exchange or IVIG) far better than to antiseizure drugs, and early treatment helps prevent cognitive decline.

det.patho: LGI1 is secreted by neurons and anchors ADAM22 and ADAM23, coupling presynaptic Kv1.1 channels to postsynaptic AMPA receptor scaffolds. IgG4 antibodies interrupt this binding, increasing neuronal excitability and reducing AMPA receptor function; complement plays a minor role. The near-universal HLA-DRB1*07:01 carriage points to a T-cell-dependent origin.
det.clinical: Typical patients are men in their sixth to eighth decade who develop extremely frequent focal seizures of several types: faciobrachial dystonic seizures, piloerection, dizziness spells, epigastric rising, fear and déjà-vu. Generalised convulsions are rare. Cognitive decline, disorientation and both anterograde and retrograde amnesia follow, and sleep disturbance and mood change are common. Hyponatraemia is a useful bedside clue. Slow presentations over years can resemble Alzheimer disease or Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.
det.diagnosis: Test serum on a cell-based assay; CSF is often negative and usually shows normal cells. The old VGKC-complex radioimmunoassay should not be used on its own, because VGKC-complex positivity without LGI1 or CASPR2 antibodies has little clinical meaning. MRI medial temporal change is present in fewer than half; EEG may be normal during FBDS. A compatible syndrome with FBDS is specific enough to start treatment while the antibody result is awaited.
det.treatment: Immunotherapy is the treatment of the seizures: steroids (IV then oral), with a low threshold for early plasma exchange or IVIG in more impaired patients. Antiseizure drugs alone rarely stop FBDS and LGI1 patients are prone to rash and Stevens-Johnson reactions, especially with aromatic drugs. Oral steroids are usually tapered slowly over about two years because short courses are linked to relapse; rituximab is used for relapse or steroid dependence.
det.prognosis: Seizures usually stop within one to three months of immunotherapy. Long-term cognition is variable: about a third recover fully, a third remain independent but cannot return to work, and a third have significant disability or die. Relapse affects 20-30% and worsens outcome. Hippocampal atrophy and persistent memory deficit are common sequelae.
pearls: FBDS that keep coming despite antiseizure drugs are an immunotherapy emergency, not a drug-dose problem.
Test serum for LGI1 — a negative CSF does not rule it out.
Unexplained hyponatraemia plus new memory loss in an older man: think LGI1.
det.thd: Anti-LGI1 ควรตรวจจากเลือดเป็นหลัก เพราะน้ำไขสันหลังให้ผลลบได้ราวครึ่งหนึ่ง ผู้ป่วยมักเป็นชายสูงอายุที่มีชักสั้นๆ ที่หน้าและแขนข้างเดียววันละหลายสิบครั้ง ตามด้วยความจำเสื่อมและโซเดียมต่ำ การชักชนิดนี้ตอบสนองต่อสเตียรอยด์และยาปรับภูมิคุ้มกันดีกว่ายากันชักมาก จึงควรรักษาเร็วเพื่อป้องกันสมองเสื่อม และค่อยๆ ลดสเตียรอยด์นานประมาณ 2 ปีเพื่อลดการกลับเป็นซ้ำ

name: Anti-CASPR2 antibody
formal: A predominantly IgG4 autoantibody against contactin-associated protein-like 2, a juxtaparanodal and synaptic adhesion molecule that clusters Kv1 channels; once grouped under 'VGKC-complex' antibodies, it marks peripheral nerve hyperexcitability, limbic encephalitis, Morvan syndrome, ataxia and neuropathic pain, almost always in older men, with thymoma in a minority.
simple: A blood test for an immune disorder of mostly older men that causes rippling, twitching or cramping muscles, burning pain, unsteadiness, sleeplessness or memory problems. Sometimes it comes from a thymus tumour, so the chest is scanned.
th: Anti-CASPR2 เป็นแอนติบอดีชนิด IgG4 ต่อโปรตีน CASPR2 เดิมจัดในกลุ่ม VGKC-complex พบเกือบทั้งหมดในชายสูงอายุ ทำให้เส้นประสาทส่วนปลายไวเกิน ปวดแสบร้อน เดินเซ สมองอักเสบส่วน limbic หรือ Morvan syndrome และอาจสัมพันธ์กับ thymoma
tempoNote: Usually evolves over months; a slow course of one to several years is common and delays diagnosis
feat: Target and class: CASPR2 at juxtaparanodes of myelinated axons and in the CNS; IgG4-dominant antibodies block CASPR2 binding to contactin-2
Who: median age mid-60s with a striking male excess (about nine men to every woman); HLA-DRB1*11:01 in most with CNS disease
Syndromes: neuromyotonia, cramps, fasciculations and myokymia; limbic encephalitis with focal seizures; Morvan syndrome; episodic or persistent ataxia
Pain: neuropathic or diffuse pain in roughly 60%, often without visible motor hyperexcitability
Tumour: thymoma in about one fifth, especially in Morvan syndrome and when LGI1 antibodies coexist
inv: Serum and CSF CASPR2-IgG by cell-based assay; low-titre serum-only results are frequent false positives — confirm with CSF, tissue-based assay or a reference laboratory
EMG/NCS: myokymic and neuromyotonic discharges, doublets and after-discharges; nerve conduction often normal
MRI brain (medial temporal change in about a third), EEG and CSF (mild pleocytosis or raised protein in a minority)
CT chest or MRI for thymoma; polysomnography if insomnia or agrypnia suggests Morvan syndrome

case.who: 71-year-old man, retired rice-mill owner from Suphan Buri
case.story: Five months of burning feet and calves, painful night cramps and constant twitching of the thighs, then three weeks of insomnia, heavy sweating and visual hallucinations at night.
case.exam: Continuous undulating myokymia of both quadriceps and calves; mild gait ataxia; disoriented to date; resting heart rate 118/min; sensation and reflexes preserved.
case.tests: EMG: myokymic and neuromyotonic discharges; serum CASPR2-IgG strongly positive and LGI1-IgG positive; CSF CASPR2-IgG positive; CT chest shows a 4 cm anterior mediastinal mass.
case.q: Which syndrome is this, and why does the mass matter for treatment?
case.a: Morvan syndrome with CASPR2 (plus LGI1) antibodies and probable thymoma; treat with immunotherapy (steroids, plasma exchange or IVIG, then rituximab if needed) and remove the thymoma, because tumour treatment is central to control.
